definition_zh: 密集的；浓密的；浓重的（雾、烟）；内容密实难懂的；质地致密的；迟钝的；单位体积质量大的
definition_en: packed closely together with little space between the parts, or containing a large amount of material in a small area
core_image: 一片密林里树干挨着树干，中间几乎插不进一只脚，抬头也看不到缝隙
scene: 清晨的山谷里，雾气厚得像一床湿棉被，二十步外的树只剩一个模糊的轮廓。A dense fog kept the whole valley invisible until noon.
sceneCN: 这里指雾气浓重、难以看透（第 2 个义项：浓重而看不透的）；句意为浓雾让整个山谷到正午都看不见。

derivatives.zh: 由表示「致密」的形容词加表示状态的名词后缀构成，义为「密度；稠密程度」
由该形容词加表示方式的副词后缀构成，义为「浓密地；密集地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词后缀构成，义为「浓密；致密性」
由该形容词的词干加表示「使……化」的动词后缀构成，义为「使致密；使加密」
同词根加表示「共同、一起」的前缀构成，义为「压缩；使变浓」，语义由「挤紧」偏移为「凝结、浓缩」
由「使变浓」的动词加表示动作结果的名词后缀构成，义为「凝结；浓缩」
由该动词加表示器械的名词后缀构成，义为「冷凝器；聚光镜」

senses.title: Packed closely in a limited space
senses.titleCN: 在有限空间里挤得很紧
senses.definition: having parts or individuals set very close together, leaving little empty space between them
senses.definitionCN: 各部分或个体彼此靠得极近，中间几乎没有空隙
senses.example: The village sits inside a dense forest of tall pines.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子坐落在一片高大松树的密林之中。
senses.why: Latin densus already meant thick or crowded, so the first sense simply states the physical packing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语中的这个词本来就表示「厚的、拥挤的」，因此第一义只是把物理上的紧密排列说出来。

senses.title: Thick enough to block the view
senses.definition: said of fog, smoke or dust that is so thick that objects behind it cannot be seen clearly
senses.definitionCN: 用于雾、烟或尘，指浓得让后面的东西看不清楚
senses.example: A dense fog delayed every flight out of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 浓雾使这座城市所有出港航班都延误了。
senses.why: A medium made of countless droplets packed close together behaves like a solid wall, so the packing sense moves to air.
senses.whyCN: 由无数微粒紧密聚成的一片介质就像一堵墙，于是「挤紧」的意思转移到了空气上。

senses.title: Carrying too much information
senses.definition: containing so many facts or ideas in a short stretch that it is hard to follow
senses.definitionCN: 在很短的篇幅里塞进太多事实或观点，因而难以跟上
senses.example: The first chapter is dense with statistics and dates.
senses.exampleCN: 第一章塞满了统计数据和日期。
senses.why: Words per page can be as tightly packed as trees in a wood, so the image of crowding is applied to text.
senses.whyCN: 每页的字数可以像林子里的树一样挤，于是「拥挤」的画面被用到了文字上。

senses.title: Slow to take in ideas
senses.definition: unable to understand things quickly, used informally and often rudely about a person
senses.definitionCN: 不能很快理解事物，口语中用来形容人，常带不客气的意味
senses.example: He is not dense; he simply needs the facts twice.
senses.exampleCN: 他并不迟钝，只是需要把事实听两遍。
senses.why: A mind that receives ideas slowly is pictured as a space too crowded for anything new to enter.
senses.whyCN: 接收想法慢的头脑，被想象成一块太挤、容不下新东西的空间。

senses.title: Heavy for its volume
senses.definition: having a high mass in relation to the space it occupies, as measured in physics
senses.definitionCN: 相对于所占体积而言质量很大，是物理上的量度说法
senses.example: Iron is dense enough to sink in water at once.
senses.exampleCN: 铁的密度足以让它立刻沉入水中。
senses.why: When matter is packed tightly, more of it fits into one cubic centimetre, which is precisely what density measures.
senses.whyCN: 物质挤得越紧，一立方厘米里装下的就越多，而密度量的正是这一点。

senses.title: Firm and solid in texture
senses.definition: having a firm, closely knit texture with few air spaces, said of bread, wood or fabric
senses.definitionCN: 质地坚实、结构紧密、内部空气少，用于面包、木材或织物
senses.example: The bakery is known for its dense rye bread.
senses.exampleCN: 这家面包店以它那款紧实的黑麦面包出名。
senses.why: Fewer air pockets mean more solid material in the same bite, so the adjective describes the inside of a loaf.
senses.whyCN: 空气孔越少，同一口里实心材料就越多，于是这个词用来形容面包的内部。

senses.title: Dark and heavy on a negative
senses.definition: showing strong deposits of silver so that the image area looks dark, used in photography
senses.definitionCN: 银盐沉积多、影像区域显得暗，是摄影中的说法
senses.example: The printer asked for a dense negative, not a thin one.
senses.exampleCN: 冲印师要的是一张浓底片，而不是薄底片。
senses.why: Photographic density counts how much silver sits in one area, the same arithmetic of packing that governs the physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 摄影中的「密度」数的是一个区域里沉积了多少银盐，与物理义遵循同一套挤紧的算术。

senses.title: Rich in content per unit
senses.definition: containing a great deal of substance or detail in proportion to its size, said approvingly of writing or art
senses.definitionCN: 相对于体量而言含有大量实质内容或细节，用于评价写作或艺术作品
senses.example: Her short essay is dense with insight on every page.
senses.exampleCN: 她那篇短文每一页都充满洞见。
senses.why: The same crowding that makes a text hard can also make it valuable when the packed material is worth reading.
senses.whyCN: 让文字难读的那种拥挤，当塞进去的材料值得一读时，也会让它变得有价值。

intro.en: Dense comes straight from Latin densus 'thick, crowded', a word used of woods, crowds and closely woven material. English took it as an adjective, and its noun density later became a measuring term in physics. The earlier Indo-European root is reconstructed, not attested.
intro.cn: dense 直接来自拉丁 densus「厚的、拥挤的」，古人用它形容树林、人群与织得很紧的织物。英语把它作为形容词引入，其名词形式 density 后来成为物理学的量度术语。更早的印欧词根属于重构形式，并未留下实证。

items.en: Densus described anything whose parts stood close together: a thick wood, a crowded street, a closely woven cloth.
items.cn: densus 形容各部分紧靠在一起的事物：茂密的树林、拥挤的街道、织得很紧的布。

items.en: The verb densare meant to make thick or to press together, and it survives in the prefixed English verbs condense and densify.
items.cn: 动词 densare 意为「使变厚、压紧」，在英语里以带前缀的形式保留下来，即 condense 与 densify。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective around the fifteenth century for thick liquids, smoke and close-grown trees; the exact first date is only approximate.
items.cn: 英语大约在十五世纪借入这个形容词，用于浓稠的液体、烟与长得密的树；确切的首见年代只是约数。

items.en: From the eighteenth century it was applied to people and buildings, giving phrases such as dense population and dense settlement.
items.cn: 十八世纪起它被用于人与建筑，产生「稠密的人口」「密集的聚落」这类说法。

items.en: The derived noun density gave science a measure of mass per volume, and photography borrowed the same noun for the blackening of a negative.
items.cn: 派生名词 density 给科学提供了单位体积质量的量度，摄影则借同一个名词表示底片的黑化程度。

items.en: In the twentieth century the adjective moved from matter to language, describing prose that packs many ideas into few lines, for praise or for complaint.
items.cn: 二十世纪这个词从物质转到语言，形容把许多想法压进几行字的文章，既可用于称赞，也可用于抱怨。

note.en: The first group shares the same stem; the second group gives neighbouring words that also describe close packing or thickness.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一个词干；第二组列出同样表示紧密或浓稠的近邻词。

entries.definition: The measurable amount of matter or information in a unit of space; the adjective describes the quality, the noun measures it.
entries.definitionCN: 单位空间内物质或信息的可测数量；形容词描述性质，名词负责计量。

entries.definition: In a closely packed manner; it modifies a verb, as in densely populated.
entries.definitionCN: 以紧密排列的方式；修饰动词，如「人口稠密地」。

entries.definition: The state of being crowded or thick; a plainer synonym of density that is rarely used in science.
entries.definitionCN: 拥挤或浓密的状态；是 density 的平实同义词，科学语境少用。

entries.definition: To make something denser, either by shrinking a text or by turning vapour into liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 使变得更密，或压缩文字，或使蒸气变成液体。

entries.definition: Deep from one surface to the other, or viscous; it measures depth or consistency, while the target word counts how many parts fill a space.
entries.definitionCN: 指从一面到另一面的厚度，或指黏稠；它量的是深度或稠度，而目标词数的是空间里装了多少部分。

entries.definition: Neatly fitted into a small space; it praises efficient arrangement, not mere crowding.
entries.definitionCN: 整齐地收在小空间里；称赞的是高效布局，而不只是拥挤。

entries.definition: Filled with people; it counts individuals in a place and says nothing about material texture.
entries.definitionCN: 充满人的；数的是一个地方里的人，不涉及材料质地。

entries.definition: Not letting light through; it describes the result of blocking light, while the target word describes the cause through packing.
entries.definitionCN: 不让光通过；描述遮光的结果，而目标词描述由紧密堆积造成的原因。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The family runs dense, densely, denseness and density.
normal.cn: 同族词包括目标词、浓密地、浓密与密度。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the physical side: dense fog, dense forest, dense crowd.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出物理一面：浓雾、密林、密集的人群。

normal.en: Science pairs the adjective with its noun: density equals mass divided by volume.
normal.cn: 科学语境把形容词与名词配成一对：密度等于质量除以体积。

normal.en: Its opposite is sparse when counting things in space, and thin when judging thickness.
normal.cn: 计数空间里的东西时反义是稀疏，判断厚薄时反义是薄。

normal.en: The stem also hides in condense, where vapour is pressed into droplets.
normal.cn: 这个词干还藏在 condense 里，那里蒸气被压成水滴。

abstract.en: Picture a subway car at rush hour where every strap is held by two hands.
abstract.cn: 想象高峰时段的地铁车厢，每条吊带都被两只手抓满。

abstract.en: Picture a sponge that holds water in every pore at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一块海绵，每一孔同时都吸满了水。

abstract.en: Picture a single page with no margin left white.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸，连一点留白都没有。

examples.en: The old quarter is dense with narrow lanes and tiny shops.
examples.cn: 老城区挤满了窄巷和小店。

examples.en: Rescue teams gave up when the smoke became too dense to see through.
examples.cn: 烟雾浓得看不透时，救援队只好放弃。

examples.en: Her notes were dense but precise, and the examiner praised them.
examples.cn: 她的笔记内容密实但精确，考官对此表示赞许。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「凳子」全都挤在一处——密不透风，就是密集

root: 拉丁 densus「厚的、拥挤的」→ 英语 dense；同族有 density、densely，带前缀的 condense 也出于同一词干。更早的印欧词根为重构形式，尚未确证。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one arithmetic: many parts inside a small space. The parts can be trees, droplets, words, ideas, silver grains or cubic centimetres of matter.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一套算术：小空间里装了很多部分。这些部分可以是树、水滴、字词、想法、银盐颗粒，也可以是一立方厘米的物质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a space so full that its parts touch, so count per volume becomes the shared measure.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个满到各部分彼此相触的空间，因此「单位体积内的数量」成为共同的量度。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL BASE: parts standing close together in a wood, a crowd or a fabric.
branches.cn: 物理基础：树林、人群或织物中各部分紧靠在一起。

branches.en: THE VISUAL EFFECT: packing so tight that light cannot pass and the view is lost.
branches.cn: 视觉效果：挤得光透不过去，视线被遮断。

branches.en: THE TEXTUAL EFFECT: too many facts per line, which makes reading slow.
branches.cn: 文本效果：每行塞入过多事实，使阅读变慢。

branches.en: THE MEASURED SIDE: a slow mind that admits no new idea, and mass counted per unit volume.
branches.cn: 可量度的一面：容不下新想法的迟钝头脑，以及按单位体积计算的质量。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL AND VALUED SIDE: firm texture, dark negatives, and content judged rich rather than merely crowded.
branches.cn: 材料与评价一面：紧实的质地、浓黑的底片，以及被评为丰厚而非仅堆砌的内容。

intro.en: Dense is a Latin adjective whose stem carries the whole family; English adds only native suffixes for state, manner and measure.
intro.cn: dense 是拉丁形容词，整个词族都由这个词干承载；英语只添加本族语后缀来表示状态、方式与量度。

latinIntro.en: Latin densus 'thick' yields the verb densare 'to make thick', whose stem gives density and the prefixed verb condense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 densus「厚的」衍生出动词 densare「使变厚」，其词干产生 density 以及带前缀的 condense。

items.structure: Latin adjective, first and second declension
items.example: The adjective describes parts standing close together.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述各部分紧靠在一起。

items.meaning: to make thick; to press together
items.example: The verb names the act of packing.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词命名「挤紧」的动作。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into the name of a measurable state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成可量度状态的名称。

items.example: The suffix marks how the packing is done.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标出挤紧的方式。

items.example: The suffix gives the plain noun for the quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀给出表示该性质的平实名词。

items.meaningCN: 单位体积的质量或数量
items.example: Physics measures density as mass over volume.
items.exampleCN: 物理学把密度计量为质量除以体积。

items.example: A densely built district has few gaps.
items.exampleCN: 建筑密集的城区几乎没有空隙。

items.example: The noun names the quality without a formula.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词不给公式，只命名性质。

items.meaning: to shrink or to turn into liquid
items.example: Cooling vapour condenses into droplets.
items.exampleCN: 蒸气冷却后凝结成水滴。

items.meaning: the act or result of condensing
items.example: The noun names the process and its product.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名过程及其产物。

items.example: The verb is used of cities and materials.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词用于城市与材料。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词的词干加表示状态的名词后缀构成，义为「密度」
由该形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「浓密地」
由该形容词加性质名词后缀构成，义为「浓密」
由词干加「使……化」的动词后缀构成，义为「使致密」
同词干加表示「共同」的前缀构成，义为「压缩；凝结」

definition_zh: 骤然而惊人的；戏剧的；夸张做作的；情节紧张的；视觉震撼的；戏剧反讽的；戏剧独白的；戏剧艺术的
definition_en: sudden and striking in effect, or belonging to the theatre and to plays
core_image: 舞台上的幕布骤然拉开，一束强光打下，演员的动作幅度大得让全场屏息
scene: 剧场的灯忽然全灭，只剩一束追光打向舞台中央，台下一片安静。The last act brought a dramatic change of fortune for the hero.
sceneCN: 这里指变化骤然而惊人（第 1 个义项：突然而剧烈、令人震动的）；句意为最后一幕让主人公的命运发生了戏剧性的转变。

derivatives.zh: 直接借自希腊语，义为「戏剧；戏剧性事件」，是该形容词的词基
由该形容词加表示方式的副词后缀构成，义为「戏剧性地；显著地」
由「戏剧」加表示从业者的后缀构成，义为「剧作家」
由「戏剧」加表示「使……化」的动词后缀构成，义为「改编成戏剧；夸大渲染」
由「改编成戏剧」的动词加表示动作结果的名词后缀构成，义为「戏剧化改编」
由「戏剧」加表示学科或活动的复数后缀构成，义为「戏剧表演；夸张做作的表现」
由「戏剧」与表示「制作、写作」的希腊成分构成，义为「戏剧创作法」

senses.title: Sudden and striking in effect
senses.definition: much greater or more sudden than expected, so that it draws strong attention
senses.definitionCN: 比预期大得多或突然得多，因而格外引人注意
senses.example: The new treatment produced a dramatic improvement in two weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 新疗法在两周内带来了显著改善。
senses.why: A play changes fortune in a single scene, and that sudden reversal is what the adjective first borrows for real events.
senses.whyCN: 戏剧在一场之内就翻转命运，这种骤然逆转正是这个词借用到现实事件上的第一层意思。

senses.title: Belonging to the theatre
senses.definition: relating to plays, acting or the writing of drama as an art form
senses.definitionCN: 与剧本、表演或戏剧创作这门艺术有关的
senses.example: She studied dramatic literature before turning to film.
senses.exampleCN: 她先研究戏剧文学，后来转向电影。
senses.why: The word is formed directly from the Greek noun for a play, so its literal sense is simply 'of drama'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词直接由希腊语中表示「戏剧」的名词构成，字面义就是「属于戏剧的」。

senses.title: Exaggerated for effect
senses.definition: behaving or expressed in an exaggerated way in order to attract attention
senses.definitionCN: 以夸张的方式表现，目的是吸引注意
senses.example: He made a dramatic exit, slamming the door behind him.
senses.exampleCN: 他夸张地退场，把门重重地摔上。
senses.why: Stage acting must reach the back row, so visible gesture becomes the model for behaviour that plays to an audience.
senses.whyCN: 舞台表演要让最后一排观众看见，于是明显外露的动作就成了「演给观众看」的行为范本。

senses.title: Full of conflict and tension
senses.definition: marked by strong conflict, suspense or emotional intensity, as a scene or event
senses.definitionCN: 带有强烈冲突、悬念或情绪张力，用于场景或事件
senses.example: The rescue became dramatic when the rope began to fray.
senses.exampleCN: 绳索开始磨断时，救援变得惊险起来。
senses.why: A stage scene holds attention through conflict, so a real situation built the same way is called dramatic.
senses.whyCN: 舞台场景靠冲突抓住注意，因此按同样方式组织的真实局面也被称为戏剧性的。

senses.title: Visually striking
senses.definition: grand or strongly contrasted in appearance, said of landscape, light or design
senses.definitionCN: 外观宏大或对比强烈，用于风景、光线或设计
senses.example: The cliffs give the coast a dramatic outline.
senses.exampleCN: 这些悬崖给了海岸线一种壮观的轮廓。
senses.why: A painted backcloth aims at strong contrast, and the adjective follows that staging into real scenery.
senses.whyCN: 手绘幕布追求强烈对比，这个词便沿着这种布景手法延伸到真实的风景。

senses.title: Irony that the audience sees
senses.titleCN: 观众看得见的戏剧反讽
senses.definition: the effect in a play where the audience knows a fact that a character does not
senses.definitionCN: 剧中观众知道某事实而人物并不知道所产生的效果
senses.example: The letter creates dramatic irony because we know who wrote it.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信造成戏剧反讽，因为我们知道是谁写的。
senses.why: The device depends on the stage separating what the audience sees from what the actor knows.
senses.whyCN: 这种手法依赖舞台把观众所见的与演员所知的隔开。

senses.title: A speech spoken by one character
senses.titleCN: 由一个人物独白的诗体
senses.definition: a poem in which a single character speaks to an implied listener at a critical moment
senses.definitionCN: 在关键时刻由单一人向隐含的听者说话的诗体
senses.example: Browning's dramatic monologue reveals the speaker's vanity.
senses.exampleCN: 勃朗宁的戏剧独白暴露了说话者的虚荣。
senses.why: One voice alone on stage carries the whole scene, and the poetic form takes its name from that staging.
senses.whyCN: 舞台上只剩一个声音承担整场戏，这种诗体便从这种舞台处理得名。

senses.title: The art of drama as a field
senses.definition: the collective field of stage and screen performance, taught and reviewed as an art
senses.definitionCN: 舞台与屏幕表演的集合门类，作为一门艺术被教授与评论
senses.example: The school offers scholarships in the dramatic arts.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校在戏剧艺术方面提供奖学金。
senses.why: Once the adjective names a whole field, it can stand before arts, literature or training as a category label.
senses.whyCN: 当这个形容词用来命名整个门类时，就可以放在艺术、文学或训练之前作分类标签。

intro.en: Dramatic goes back to Greek drama 'a deed, an action', from dran 'to do'. Greek dramatikos meant 'of action, of the stage', and English took the adjective through Latin and French in the sixteenth century. The chain of derivation is well recorded; only the earliest first-use date is approximate.
intro.cn: dramatic 上溯希腊语 drama「行为、行动」，源自动词 dran「做」。希腊语 dramatikos 意为「行动的、舞台的」，英语十六世纪经拉丁语与法语引入这个形容词。构词链记录清楚，只有最早的使用年代是约数。

items.en: The verb dran meant to do or to act, and it supplied the noun for a thing done rather than for a written text.
items.cn: 动词 dran 意为「做、行动」，它衍生出的名词指「做成的事」，起初并不指写下来的文本。

items.en: Drama first named a deed or an action; because a staged play is a series of actions, the word became the name of the play itself.
items.cn: drama 最初指行为或行动；由于上演的戏就是一串行动，这个词随后成为剧本与戏剧的名称。

items.en: The adjective dramatikos meant 'skilled in acting' or 'belonging to action', and it described both the poet and the art.
items.cn: 形容词 dramatikos 意为「擅长行动的」或「属于行动的」，既形容剧作家也形容这门艺术。

items.en: Latin drama and French dramatique carried the Greek word westward; Latin added no new root of its own.
items.cn: 拉丁语 drama 与法语 dramatique 把希腊词向西传递；拉丁语本身没有添加新的词根。

items.en: English dramatic appears in the sixteenth century for what belongs to plays, and soon extends to real events that look staged.
items.cn: 英语的这个词在十六世纪出现，指属于戏剧的事物，很快又扩展到看上去像舞台上演的真实事件。

items.en: Dramatic irony, dramatic monologue and dramatic arts are fixed terms; the looser sense 'striking' is a later everyday extension.
items.cn: 「戏剧反讽」「戏剧独白」「戏剧艺术」都是固定术语；较松散的「引人注目」义是后来在日常用语中扩展出来的。

note.en: The first group is the same family of stage words; the second group holds adjectives that also describe strong effect.
note.cn: 第一组是同一族舞台用语；第二组是同样描述强烈效果的形容词。

entries.definition: A play, or the art of plays; the noun names the work, while the adjective describes what belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 戏剧作品或戏剧艺术；名词指作品本身，形容词指属于它的。

entries.definition: In a striking or theatrical manner; it tells how a change happened.
entries.definitionCN: 以惊人方式或以戏剧化方式；说明变化是如何发生的。

entries.definition: A writer of plays; the suffix marks the person, not the quality.
entries.definitionCN: 剧作家；后缀标出从事的人，而非性质。

entries.definition: To turn a story into a play, or to make an event seem more striking than it was.
entries.definitionCN: 把故事改编成戏剧，或把事件渲染得比实际更惊人。

entries.definition: Belonging to the theatre, often with a hint of showing off; it stresses performance, while the target word stresses striking effect.
entries.definitionCN: 属于剧场的，常带「做给人看」的意味；强调表演性，而目标词强调效果惊人。

entries.definition: Extreme and severe, said of measures; it stresses harshness rather than visual or emotional impact.
entries.definitionCN: 极端的、严厉的，用于措施；强调严厉，而非视觉或情绪冲击。

entries.definition: Attracting attention at once; it is the calm general word, without the stage metaphor.
entries.definitionCN: 立刻引人注意；是平实的通用词，不带舞台隐喻。

entries.definition: Happening without warning; it only marks timing, while the target word adds scale and effect.
entries.definitionCN: 毫无预警地发生；只标时间，而目标词还带上规模与效果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The word is the adjective of drama, so it literally means 'of a play'.
normal.cn: 这个词是「戏剧」的形容词，字面就是「属于戏的」。

normal.en: The family runs drama, dramatist, dramatize and dramatically.
normal.cn: 同族词包括戏剧、剧作家、改编成戏剧与戏剧性地。

normal.en: Fixed terms keep the stage sense: dramatic irony, dramatic monologue, dramatic arts.
normal.cn: 固定术语保留舞台义：戏剧反讽、戏剧独白、戏剧艺术。

normal.en: Fixed phrases keep the effect sense: dramatic change, dramatic improvement, dramatic effect.
normal.cn: 固定搭配保留效果义：剧变、显著改善、戏剧性效果。

normal.en: Greek dran 'to do' is the root: a play is a series of deeds, not a printed book.
normal.cn: 希腊语 dran「做」是词根：戏是一连串行动，不是一叠印好的书。

abstract.en: Picture one spotlight moving while everything else stays dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏追光在移动，其余一切保持黑暗。

abstract.en: Picture a door slammed so hard that the whole hall hears it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门被摔得整个大厅都听见。

abstract.en: Picture a single actor holding an empty stage for one long minute.
abstract.cn: 想象一个演员在空舞台上独撑整整一分钟。

examples.en: The patient's recovery in three days was dramatic.
examples.cn: 病人三天内的康复很惊人。

examples.en: Her dramatic reading of the letter made the room go silent.
examples.cn: 她把那封信读得极具戏剧性，全场安静下来。

examples.en: The valley looks dramatic from the ridge at sunset.
examples.cn: 日落时从山脊看这道山谷，景色十分壮观。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抓马」——戏台上的抓马场面，就是戏剧性的

root: 希腊 dran「做、行动」→ drama「行动、戏剧」→ dramatikos「戏剧的」→ 拉丁 drama 与法语 dramatique → 英语 dramatic。构词链完整，词源无争议。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses branch from one root idea: a play is a chain of deeds. That gives the theatre senses, and also the everyday sense of any change that lands like a stage reversal.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一个根想法分出：戏是一连串行动。由此得到各戏剧义项，也得到日常中「像舞台逆转一样」的各种变化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one strong action under a spotlight, which either belongs to a play or hits real life like a scene.
core.cn: 核心意象：追光下的一记强动作，它或属于剧本，或像一幕戏那样砸进现实。

branches.en: THE ROOT SENSE: whatever belongs to plays and acting as an art.
branches.cn: 本根义：属于剧本与表演艺术的一切。

branches.en: THE VOICE: one character alone speaking at a decisive moment.
branches.cn: 声音：一个人物在关键时刻独自陈说。

branches.en: THE STRUCTURE: rising conflict, and irony built on what the audience knows.
branches.cn: 结构：不断上升的冲突，以及建立在观众所知之上的反讽。

branches.en: THE REAL-LIFE SPILL: sudden reversals that shock, and gesture exaggerated to be seen.
branches.cn: 漫出戏外：令人震动的骤变，以及为被看见而夸张的姿态。

branches.en: THE VISIBLE AND THE INSTITUTIONAL: strong visual contrast, and the whole field of dramatic arts.
branches.cn: 可见与建制：强烈视觉对比，以及戏剧艺术这一整个门类。

intro.en: Dramatic is a Greek word carried into English by Latin and French, with a Greek noun base and a Greek adjective ending.
intro.cn: dramatic 是经拉丁语与法语进入英语的希腊词，由希腊语名词词基与希腊语形容词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin holds only the borrowed form drama, used in transmission; it contributes no root of its own, so the Latin entry list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语只保留借来的形式 drama，仅起传递作用，并未贡献自己的词根，因此拉丁词条列表留空。

items.example: The verb names the deed behind every scene.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词命名每场戏背后的行动。

items.example: The noun shifted from deed to staged play.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词从「行为」转为「上演的戏」。

items.example: The adjective described both poet and art.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词既形容剧作家也形容艺术。

items.example: The ending makes the adjective of drama.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾造出「属于戏剧的」形容词。

items.example: The ending gives the manner adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾给出方式副词。

items.example: English added the everyday sense of striking.
items.exampleCN: 英语又加上了「惊人」这一日常义。

items.example: The suffix marks the person who writes.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标出写作的人。

items.example: The verb turns a story into a play.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把故事变成戏剧。

items.example: The plural noun can also mean exaggerated behaviour.
items.exampleCN: 这个复数名词也可指夸张的表现。

items.example: The adverb often modifies verbs of change.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词常修饰表示变化的动词。

derivatives.zh: 直接借自希腊语，义为「戏剧」，是该形容词的词基
由该形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「戏剧性地；显著地」
由「戏剧」加表示从业者的后缀构成，义为「剧作家」
由「戏剧」加「使……化」的动词后缀构成，义为「改编成戏剧」
由「戏剧」加学科或活动后缀构成，义为「戏剧表演；做作的表现」

definition_zh: 精工细作的；装饰繁复的；复杂冗长的；精心筹备的；详细说明；进一步阐发；逐步构建；澄清式详述
definition_en: made with many carefully arranged details, or to explain something by adding more and more detail
core_image: 老工匠在灯下给一只木匣雕出一层层花纹，连抽屉内侧也刻满细密的纹路
scene: 作坊里，老师傅把一只木匣拆成十几道工序，每一道都要再打磨一遍才肯装上去。The curator gave an elaborate account of how the box was made.
sceneCN: 这里指内容繁复、细节层层叠加的（第 1 个义项：由大量精心加工的细节构成）；句意为馆长对这只匣子的制作过程作了极为繁复的说明。

pos.zh: 精工细作的；繁复的；复杂冗长的
详细说明；进一步阐发；逐步构建

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示方式的副词后缀构成，义为「精细地；繁复地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词后缀构成，义为「繁复；精细程度」
由「详细说明、精心制作」的动词加表示动作结果的名词后缀构成，义为「详述；精心加工」
拉丁词根「劳动」，是该词后半部分的直接来源，义为「劳动；劳作」

senses.title: Made with many worked-out details
senses.titleCN: 由大量精心加工的细节做成
senses.definition: built or arranged with a great many carefully finished parts, each receiving attention
senses.definitionCN: 由许许多多仔细完成的部件构成，每一处都得到照料
senses.example: The cabinet has an elaborate system of hidden drawers.
senses.exampleCN: 这只柜子有一套精巧的暗抽屉结构。
senses.why: Latin elaboratus meant 'worked out', so the adjective starts as a report on how much work went in.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的拉丁语来源本是「已经做出来的」之意，因此这个形容词起初是在说明花了多少工夫。

senses.title: Richly ornamented
senses.definition: decorated with many small ornamental elements rather than left plain
senses.definitionCN: 饰有许多细小装饰元素，而非保持素净
senses.example: The bride wore an elaborate headdress of silver wire.
senses.exampleCN: 新娘戴着一顶银丝编成的繁复头饰。
senses.why: Ornament is added detail, so the sense of many worked parts is applied to surface decoration.
senses.whyCN: 装饰就是额外加上去的细节，于是「许多加工过的小部件」这层意思被用到表面装饰上。

senses.title: Complicated and drawn out
senses.definition: having many steps or conditions, so that it takes longer than expected, often with a hint of excess
senses.definitionCN: 步骤或条件很多，因而比预期更久，常带「过于繁琐」的意味
senses.example: Getting a permit required an elaborate procedure of stamps and signatures.
senses.exampleCN: 办许可证要经过一套繁琐的盖章签字程序。
senses.why: When details multiply without need, the same word shifts from praise to complaint.
senses.whyCN: 当细节不必要地层层增加时，同一个词就从称赞转为抱怨。

senses.title: Prepared through many stages
senses.definition: planned and prepared with many separate stages, said of meals, ceremonies or receptions
senses.definitionCN: 经许多独立环节筹划准备，用于宴席、仪式或招待会
senses.example: They staged an elaborate dinner for the retiring professor.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为这位退休教授办了一场精心筹备的晚宴。
senses.why: A long menu of separately prepared dishes shows the same many-stage labour on a table.
senses.whyCN: 一道道单独准备的菜，把同样的多道工序劳动摆到了餐桌上。

senses.title: To explain with more detail
senses.definition: to add further details to something already said so that the listener understands it fully
senses.definitionCN: 对已经说过的内容补充更多细节，使听者完全理解
senses.example: Could you elaborate on the second point?
senses.exampleCN: 你能把第二点再详细说明一下吗？
senses.why: The verb keeps the Latin image of working something out, now applied to ideas rather than wood.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了拉丁语「把某物做出来」的画面，只是材料从木头换成了想法。

senses.title: To develop an idea into a full account
senses.titleCN: 把想法展开成完整论述
senses.definition: to expand a brief statement or proposal into a connected argument with supporting parts
senses.definitionCN: 把简短的陈述或设想扩展成有支撑部分的连贯论证
senses.example: The paper elaborates a model of urban growth over ten pages.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文用十页篇幅展开了一个城市增长模型。
senses.why: Developing a theory resembles building a cabinet: small parts are fitted until the whole stands.
senses.whyCN: 发展一套理论就像做柜子：小部件一件件装上，直到整体立起来。

senses.title: To build up step by step
senses.definition: to construct something gradually by adding and fitting parts until it is complete
senses.definitionCN: 通过不断添加、拼合部件逐步建成完整之物
senses.example: The composer elaborated the theme into a full symphony.
senses.exampleCN: 作曲家把这个主题逐步铺展成一部完整的交响曲。
senses.why: The prefix meant 'out' and the root meant 'labour', so the verb pictures work that draws a thing out into being.
senses.whyCN: 前缀意为「出」，词根意为「劳作」，所以这个动词画出的是「把东西一点点做出来」的过程。

senses.title: To spell out in order to prevent doubt
senses.titleCN: 为消除疑问而逐条说清
senses.definition: to state details explicitly so that no ambiguity or misunderstanding remains
senses.definitionCN: 把细节明确说出来，使不再有歧义或误解
senses.example: The lawyer elaborated the terms before anyone signed.
senses.exampleCN: 律师在任何人签字之前把条款逐条说清。
senses.why: Explicit detail removes gaps, and gaps are exactly what the crowding of parts fills in.
senses.whyCN: 明确的细节填掉了空白，而「部件密集」填补的正是这些空白。

intro.en: Elaborate comes from Latin elaborare 'to labour out, to work up', built from ex- 'out' and laborare 'to work', from labor 'toil'. Its past participle elaboratus gave English the adjective 'worked out, highly finished'. The verb entered English in the sixteenth century and the adjective soon after; only the earliest dates are approximate.
intro.cn: elaborate 出自拉丁 elaborare「做出来、精心做成」，由 ex-「出」与 laborare「劳作」构成，后者源于 labor「辛劳」。其过去分词 elaboratus 给英语带来「精心做出的、完成度高的」这一形容词义。动词十六世纪进入英语，形容词紧随其后；最早年代只是约数。

items.en: Labor meant toil, effort or hardship, and it is the source of the English noun labour as well.
items.cn: labor 意为辛劳、努力或艰难，也是英语名词 labour 的来源。

items.en: The verb laborare meant to work or to take pains, and it described steady effort rather than a single act.
items.cn: 动词 laborare 意为劳作或费心，描述的是一段持续的努力，而不是一次性的动作。

items.en: With ex- 'out', elaborare meant to work something out or to produce it with care, the image of effort drawing a result into being.
items.cn: 加上表示「出」的前缀后，elaborare 意为把某物做出来或精心制作，画面是「用力把成果拉出来」。

items.en: The past participle elaboratus described a finished thing, one that had been thoroughly worked, and this is the direct source of the adjective.
items.cn: 过去分词 elaboratus 形容已完成、被彻底加工过的东西，这正是形容词的直接来源。

items.en: The verb arrived in the sixteenth century meaning to produce by labour, and later narrowed to developing an idea in speech or writing.
items.cn: 动词十六世纪进入英语，意为「通过劳作生产出来」，后来收窄为在口语或写作中展开一个想法。

items.en: The adjective kept the participle sense of 'highly finished' and then divided into praise for fine detail and complaint about too many steps.
items.cn: 形容词保留分词「完成度高」的意思，随后分为两支：称赞细节精美，以及抱怨环节太多。

note.en: The first group shares the labour stem; the second group holds adjectives for complexity and fine detail, each with a different centre.
note.cn: 第一组共享「劳作」词干；第二组是表示复杂与精细的形容词，各自的侧重不同。

entries.definition: The act of explaining further or of adding worked detail; the noun names the process or its result.
entries.definitionCN: 进一步说明或添加加工细节的行为；名词指过程或结果。

entries.definition: In a detailed or ornate manner; it tells how something was made or said.
entries.definitionCN: 以繁复精细的方式；说明制作或陈述的方式。

entries.definition: The quality of having many worked details; a state noun rather than a process noun.
entries.definitionCN: 具有许多加工细节的性质；是状态名词而非过程名词。

entries.definition: Hard work; the root word behind the whole verb, still used on its own.
entries.definitionCN: 艰苦的劳动；整个动词背后的词根，至今独立使用。

entries.definition: Containing many facts or features; it merely reports abundance of detail, without judging the labour behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 含有很多事实或特征；只说明细节多，不评价背后的工夫。

entries.definition: Having parts interwoven so that they are hard to trace; it stresses entanglement rather than finish.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分交织而难以理清；强调缠绕难解，而非完成度。

entries.definition: Heavily decorated; it applies only to surface ornament, never to plans or explanations.
entries.definitionCN: 装饰繁重的；只用于表面装饰，不用于计划或说明。

entries.definition: Hard to understand because of many linked parts; it stresses difficulty, not craftsmanship.
entries.definitionCN: 因关联部分多而难懂；强调困难，而不强调工艺。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means 'out' and the root means 'labour': to elaborate is to labour a thing out.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「出」，词根意为「劳作」：详述就是把东西一点点做出来。

normal.en: The family runs elaborate, elaborately, elaborateness and elaboration.
normal.cn: 同族词包括目标词、精细地、繁复与详述。

normal.en: The adjective takes more and most, since it is long: more elaborate, most elaborate.
normal.cn: 这个形容词较长，比较级与最高级用 more 与 most 构成。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the two sides: elaborate design and elaborate procedure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分出两面：精巧的设计，与繁琐的程序。

normal.en: The verb is followed by on: to elaborate on a point is to add detail to it.
normal.cn: 动词后接 on：对某一点作进一步说明，就是给它添细节。

abstract.en: Picture a gift box wrapped in eleven layers of paper, each a different colour.
abstract.cn: 想象一只礼盒包了十一层纸，每层颜色都不同。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose face is covered by tiny painted birds.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟，表盘上密布手绘的小鸟。

abstract.en: Picture one sentence growing into a page without losing its thread.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话长成一整页，却始终没有丢掉主线。

examples.en: The wedding cake was elaborate, with sugar flowers on every tier.
examples.cn: 婚礼蛋糕十分繁复，每一层都有糖花。

examples.en: He refused to elaborate on why he had resigned.
examples.cn: 他拒绝进一步说明辞职的原因。

examples.en: Their plan was too elaborate to survive a single delay.
examples.cn: 他们的计划过于繁复，一次延误就撑不住。

root: 拉丁 labor「辛劳」→ laborare「劳作」→ elaborare「精心做出」→ 过去分词 elaboratus 作形容词 → 英语 elaborate。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses grow from one picture: work that draws a thing out part by part. Applied to objects it means finely worked; applied to words it means detail added until the idea stands complete.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项出自同一幅画：用工夫把东西一件件做出来。用于物件指精工细作；用于言语指不断添细节，直到想法完整立起。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: patient labour adding one fitted part after another until the whole is finished.
core.cn: 核心意象：耐心的劳作，一件接一件地装上合适的部件，直到整体完成。

branches.en: THE WORKED OBJECT: many carefully finished parts inside one thing.
branches.cn: 被加工的物件：一件东西里有许多仔细完成的部件。

branches.en: THE ORNAMENT LAYER: added decoration, where detail sits on the surface.
branches.cn: 装饰层：额外添加的装饰，细节停在表面上。

branches.en: THE DRAWN-OUT SIDE: procedures with too many steps, and meals or rites prepared in many stages.
branches.cn: 冗长的一面：步骤过多的程序，以及经多道工序准备的宴席与仪式。

branches.en: THE SPOKEN SIDE: adding detail to a statement and expanding it into a full argument.
branches.cn: 言语一面：为陈述添细节，并把它扩展成完整论证。

branches.en: THE CONSTRUCTIVE SIDE: building something step by step, and spelling terms out so no doubt remains.
branches.cn: 构建一面：一步步搭成某物，以及把条款逐条说清以消除疑问。

intro.en: Elaborate is built on the Latin noun labor 'toil', its verb laborare, and the prefix ex- 'out'; English adds endings for manner, state and action.
intro.cn: elaborate 建立在拉丁名词 labor「辛劳」、其动词 laborare 与表示「出」的前缀 ex- 之上；英语再添加表示方式、状态与动作的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin labor 'toil' gives laborare 'to work'; ex- 'out' plus laborare gives elaborare 'to work out'; the participle elaboratus gives the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 labor「辛劳」给出 laborare「劳作」；ex-「出」加 laborare 得出 elaborare「做出来」；分词 elaboratus 给出形容词。

items.example: The noun names the effort behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名整个词族背后的努力。

items.example: The verb describes steady effort.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描述持续的努力。

items.example: The prefix shows the result being drawn out.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀表示成果被「做出来」。

items.meaning: to work out; to produce with care
items.example: The compound verb adds the idea of completion.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词加上了「完成」之意。

items.meaningCN: 精心做成的；完成度高的
items.example: The participle became the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词成了英语形容词。

items.example: The ending serves both the verb and the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾同时服务动词与形容词。

items.example: The suffix marks how the work was done.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标出制作的方式。

items.example: The suffix names the quality of richness in detail.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名细节繁复的性质。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成过程名词。

items.example: The adverb often modifies made or decorated.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词常修饰「制作」「装饰」一类动词。

items.example: The noun covers both the spoken and made sides.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词同时覆盖言语与制作两面。

由该形容词加性质名词后缀构成，义为「繁复」
由该动词加动作名词后缀构成，义为「详述；精心加工」

definition_zh: 必不可少的；本质的；提炼的（精油）；要点；必需品；必要条件；本质属性；关键服务的
definition_en: absolutely necessary, or belonging to the very nature of a thing
core_image: 一只果子被层层剥开，最里面那颗小小的核始终不动，其余部分都可以拿走
scene: 实验室里，学生把一筐花瓣放进蒸馏器，收集瓶里浮起薄薄一层无色油。The recipe needs only a few drops of essential oil from lavender.
sceneCN: 这里指从植物中提炼出的精华油（第 3 个义项：植物体内精华部分的浓缩提取物）；句意为这道配方只需几滴薰衣草精油。

pos.zh: 必不可少的；本质的；基本的

derivatives.zh: 直接来自拉丁 essentia「本质」，是该形容词的词基，义为「本质；精华」
由该形容词加表示方式的副词后缀构成，义为「本质上；基本上」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词后缀构成，义为「必要性；本质性」
由该形容词加表示学说体系的名词后缀构成，义为「本质主义」
由「本质主义」加表示主张者的后缀构成，义为「本质主义者；本质主义的」
由表示「第五」的拉丁成分与「本质」复合而成，义为「精髓；典范」，因古人把第五种元素视为万物精华

senses.title: Absolutely necessary
senses.definition: so necessary that the purpose cannot be achieved without it
senses.definitionCN: 必要到缺了它就无法达到目的的程度
senses.example: Clean water is essential for every village here.
senses.exampleCN: 清洁的水对这里每个村庄都必不可少。
senses.why: If something belongs to a thing's essence, removing it destroys the thing, so 'of the essence' naturally means 'cannot be done without'.
senses.whyCN: 若某物属于事物的本质，去掉它就毁了该事物，因此「属于本质」自然引申为「不可缺少」。

senses.title: Belonging to the nature of a thing
senses.definition: forming part of what a thing fundamentally is, rather than an accidental feature
senses.definitionCN: 构成某物根本之所是，而非偶然附带的特征
senses.example: Risk is essential to exploration, not a flaw in it.
senses.exampleCN: 风险是探索的本性，而不是它的缺陷。
senses.why: The word was coined to name being itself, so the adjective first marks what something is, not what it happens to have.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原本是为命名「存在」本身而造，因此形容词首先标出某物「是什么」，而不是它恰好有什么。

senses.title: The concentrated extract of a plant
senses.definition: a volatile oil that carries the characteristic fragrance or active principle of a plant
senses.definitionCN: 携带植物特有香气或活性成分的挥发性油
senses.example: Two drops of essential oil scent the whole room.
senses.exampleCN: 两滴精油就能让整个房间充满香气。
senses.why: Ancient chemistry held that a fifth essence underlay all matter; the oil that carries a plant's character inherits that name.
senses.whyCN: 古代化学认为万物之下有第五种精华元素；携带植物特性的油便承袭了这一说法。

senses.title: The points that must be learned
senses.definition: the small set of central facts or rules that a subject cannot be understood without
senses.definitionCN: 一门学问缺了就无法理解的那一小撮核心事实或规则
senses.example: The primer covers the essentials of grammar in forty pages.
senses.exampleCN: 这本入门书用四十页讲完语法要点。
senses.why: A subject has an essence too, and its essentials are the parts that carry it.
senses.whyCN: 一门学问也有其本质，它的「要点」正是承载这一本质的部分。

senses.title: The things one cannot travel without
senses.definition: the basic items needed for a particular activity or situation, usually plural
senses.definitionCN: 某项活动或情境所需的基本物品，通常用复数
senses.example: Pack only the essentials: passport, medicine and a charger.
senses.exampleCN: 只带必需品：护照、药品和充电器。
senses.why: What is necessary for a purpose is concrete here, so the plural noun lists the objects themselves.
senses.whyCN: 为某个目的所必需之物在这里变得具体，于是复数名词直接列出这些物件。

senses.title: Required as a prior condition
senses.definition: demanded as a condition that must be met before something else can happen
senses.definitionCN: 作为必须先满足的条件而被要求
senses.example: Attendance at the safety course is essential before lab work.
senses.exampleCN: 进实验室之前，必须参加安全课程。
senses.why: A prior condition is part of the definition of the later step, so it counts as belonging to its essence.
senses.whyCN: 先决条件构成后一步骤定义的一部分，因此也算「属于其本质」。

senses.title: Essence as a philosophical category
senses.titleCN: 哲学意义上的本质属性
senses.definition: the set of properties that make a thing the kind of thing it is, as opposed to accidental ones
senses.definitionCN: 使某物成为该类事物的那些属性，与偶然属性相对
senses.example: The lecture asked whether reason is essential to being human.
senses.exampleCN: 这场讲座追问理性是否属于人的本质。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: the word was invented to translate the Greek notion of what a thing truly is.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：这个词正是为翻译希腊语中「某物真正是什么」的概念而造。

senses.title: Sustaining the basic life of a society
senses.definition: said of workers or services that must keep running even in a crisis
senses.definitionCN: 用于危机中也必须持续运转的人员或服务
senses.example: Hospitals and water plants are essential services.
senses.exampleCN: 医院与自来水厂属于基本公共服务。
senses.why: A society has essentials too: the functions that, if removed, stop everything else.
senses.whyCN: 社会也有其「本质」：一旦撤掉就会让其余一切停摆的那些功能。

intro.en: Essential rests on Latin esse 'to be'. Cicero coined essentia to render Greek ousia 'being, essence', and Late Latin essentialis gave English the adjective. The word therefore began as a philosophical term and only later became the everyday word for 'necessary'. First records are approximate.
intro.cn: essential 建立在拉丁 esse「存在、是」之上。西塞罗造 essentia 来翻译希腊语 ousia「存在、本质」，晚期拉丁 essentialis 给出英语形容词。因此这个词最初是哲学术语，后来才成为日常表示「必要」的词。首见年代均为约数。

items.en: Esse meant to be or to exist, and its participle stem essent- supplied the base of the whole family.
items.cn: esse 意为「是、存在」，其分词词干 essent- 提供了整个词族的基础。

items.en: Lacking a Latin word for Greek ousia, Cicero coined essentia, literally 'the state of being', and the coinage entered philosophy.
items.cn: 由于拉丁语没有对应希腊语 ousia 的词，西塞罗造了 essentia，字面为「存在的状态」，这一新造词进入哲学。

items.en: Essentialis meant 'of the essence', describing what belongs to a thing's being rather than to its accidents.
items.cn: essentialis 意为「属于本质的」，描述属于事物存在本身而非偶然属性的东西。

items.en: English took the adjective in the fourteenth century, first in theology and philosophy, where essence and accident were technical pairs.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪引入这个形容词，最初用于神学与哲学，那里「本质」与「偶然属性」是成对的术语。

items.en: Because what belongs to a essence cannot be removed, the adjective drifted toward 'necessary', which is now its most common everyday use.
items.cn: 由于属于本质的东西不能被去掉，这个形容词逐渐偏向「必要」，如今这已是它最常见的日常用法。

items.en: Alchemists spoke of a fifth essence beyond the four elements; an oil that carries a plant's scent and virtue was called its essential oil.
items.cn: 炼金术士谈到四种元素之外的第五种精华；携带植物香气与药性的油便被称为它的精油。

note.en: The first group shares the being stem; the second group holds words for importance, each with a different reason.
note.cn: 第一组共享「存在」词干；第二组是表示重要的词，各自的理由不同。

entries.definition: The inner nature of a thing; the noun names what the adjective describes as belonging to it.
entries.definitionCN: 事物的内在本性；名词命名形容词所说「属于它」的那个东西。

entries.definition: Fundamentally, or in the main; it often means 'when everything is considered'.
entries.definitionCN: 本质上，或大体上；常表示「把一切算进去之后」。

entries.definition: The doctrine that things have fixed essential natures; a philosophical noun, not a synonym of necessity.
entries.definitionCN: 认为事物有固定本质的学说；是哲学术语，不是「必要性」的同义词。

entries.definition: The purest representative of something; it joins 'fifth' to the same essence root.
entries.definitionCN: 某物最纯粹的典范；把「第五」与同一「本质」词根连接起来。

entries.definition: Required for a result; the neutral word, without the hint that the thing belongs to a nature.
entries.definitionCN: 为达成结果所需；语气中性，不含「属于本性」的意味。

entries.definition: Needed for life or success; it stresses survival and urgency, not definition.
entries.definitionCN: 为生命或成败所需；强调存亡与紧迫，而不强调定义。

entries.definition: Lying at the base of a system; it stresses position in a structure rather than indispensability.
entries.definitionCN: 位于体系底层的；强调结构中的位置，而非不可缺。

entries.definition: Impossible to do without or replace; it adds the idea that no substitute exists.
entries.definitionCN: 无法省去或替代；多了「找不到替代品」这层意思。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root is the Latin verb 'to be': the essence is what a thing is.
normal.cn: 词根是拉丁语「存在」动词：本质就是某物之所是。

normal.en: The family runs essence, essentially, essentiality and essentialism.
normal.cn: 同族词包括本质、基本上、必要性、本质主义。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the necessary side: essential services, essential goods, essential condition.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出必要一面：基本公共服务、必需商品、必要条件。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the nature side: essential difference, essential feature.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出本性一面：本质区别、本质特征。

normal.en: The plural noun means the short list you cannot leave behind.
normal.cn: 复数名词指那张你离不开的短清单。

abstract.en: Picture a fruit whose skin, flesh and juice can all be peeled away, leaving one hard stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一只果子，皮、肉、汁都能剥掉，最后只剩一颗硬核。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge with one stone that holds every arch in place.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥，有一块石头撑住了所有拱。

abstract.en: Picture a suitcase packed only with the four things you truly need.
abstract.cn: 想象一只行李箱，只装了四件真正需要的东西。

examples.en: Trust is essential to any long partnership.
examples.cn: 信任对任何长期合作都必不可少。

examples.en: The course teaches the essentials of statistical design.
examples.cn: 这门课讲授统计设计的要点。

examples.en: Fewer nurses would leave the ward without its essential staff.
examples.cn: 少了骨干人员，这个病房就撑不下去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一森舍」——整片森林都可以舍掉，只留下最里面那一层，就是本质

root: 拉丁 esse「是、存在」→ 分词词干 essent- → 西塞罗造 essentia「本质」→ 晚期拉丁 essentialis → 英语 essential。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one question: what is at the core? The core may be a thing's nature, a plant's fragrance, a subject's key points, or the single item you cannot do without.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个追问：核在哪里？这个核可以是事物的本性、植物的香气、学问的要点，也可以是那件缺了就不行的事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone at the centre of a fruit that survives after everything else is peeled away.
core.cn: 核心意象：果子中央的一颗硬核，其余部分都剥掉之后它仍在。

branches.en: THE OLDEST LAYER: essence as a philosophical category opposed to accident.
branches.cn: 最古老的一层：作为哲学范畴的本质，与偶然属性相对。

branches.en: THE NATURE SENSE: belonging to what a thing fundamentally is.
branches.cn: 本性义：属于某物根本之所是。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL EXTRACT: the oil that carries a plant's character.
branches.cn: 物质提取：承载植物特性的精油。

branches.en: THE SHORT LIST: key points of a subject and the basic items one packs.
branches.cn: 短清单：一门学问的要点，以及出行所带的基本物品。

branches.en: THE INDISPENSABLE SIDE: what cannot be done without, a prior condition, and services a society must keep running.
branches.cn: 不可缺一面：缺了就不行之物、先决条件，以及社会必须维持运转的服务。

intro.en: Essential is built on the Latin verb 'to be' plus a state noun ending and an adjective ending; its Latin history is unusually well documented because Cicero recorded the coinage.
intro.cn: essential 建立在拉丁语「存在」动词之上，再加表示状态的名词词尾与形容词词尾；由于西塞罗留下了造词的记录，它的拉丁语历史格外清楚。

latinIntro.en: Latin esse 'to be' gives essentia 'being'; essentia plus -alis gives essentialis; French and English carry the adjective onward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 esse「存在」给出 essentia「存在、本质」；essentia 加 -alis 得出 essentialis；法语与英语把这个形容词继续传下去。

items.example: The verb is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的根。

items.example: The stem carries the idea of being.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载「存在」的观念。

items.example: Cicero coined it for Greek philosophy.
items.exampleCN: 西塞罗为希腊哲学造出这个词。

items.example: The ending makes an adjective of essence.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把「本质」变成形容词。

items.example: The Late Latin adjective entered philosophy.
items.exampleCN: 这个晚期拉丁形容词进入哲学。

items.example: English added the everyday sense of necessity.
items.exampleCN: 英语加上了日常的「必要」义。

items.example: The suffix gives the adverb meaning 'fundamentally'.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀给出「本质上」的副词。

items.example: The suffix names the quality of being necessary.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名「必要性」这一性质。

items.example: The suffix builds the name of a philosophical school.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀造出一个哲学流派的名字。

items.meaning: the fifth essence; the purest part
items.meaningCN: 第五种精华；最纯粹的部分
items.example: Alchemy pictured a fifth element beyond the four.
items.exampleCN: 炼金术设想四种元素之外的第五种。

由该形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「本质上」
由该形容词加性质名词后缀构成，义为「必要性」

definition_zh: 数量过多的；强度过大的；价格过高的；过分夸赞的；越权的；反应过激的；医学上的过度；文体上过度修饰的
definition_en: more than is reasonable, proper or necessary, whether in amount, force, price or behaviour
core_image: 一只碗已经盛到碗沿，勺子还在往里倒，汤沿着碗壁流到桌上
scene: 宴会散场后，后厨的垃圾桶里堆满几乎没动过的菜，服务员还在往外端新的盘子。The caterer was blamed for the excessive amount of food left untouched.
sceneCN: 这里指数量超出实际需要（第 1 个义项：数目或分量多得不合理）；句意为承办方因剩下大量没动过的食物而受指责。

derivatives.zh: 直接来自拉丁 excessus「越界、过度」，是该形容词的词基，义为「过量；超额的」
由该形容词加表示方式的副词后缀构成，义为「过度地；过分地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词后缀构成，义为「过度；过分」
由同一拉丁动词的另一条路径进入英语，义为「超过；越过」，与目标词共享「走出界线」的词根

senses.title: More in amount than is needed
senses.definition: present in a quantity larger than the purpose requires, so that some of it is wasted
senses.definitionCN: 数量超过目的所需，因而有一部分被浪费
senses.example: The report criticized the excessive use of paper in the office.
senses.exampleCN: 报告批评了办公室纸张使用过量的问题。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to go beyond a boundary, so the first sense simply states that the amount has crossed the line.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「走出界线」，因此第一义只是说数量越过了那条线。

senses.title: Stronger in force than allowed
senses.definition: applied with more physical force or intensity than the situation permits
senses.definitionCN: 施加的体力或强度超过情境所允许的程度
senses.example: The officers were accused of using excessive force at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 这些警员被指在大门处使用了过度武力。
senses.why: Force also has a permitted boundary, and anything past it is described by the same verb of overstepping.
senses.whyCN: 武力也有许可的边界，越过这条边界的都用同一个「越界」动词来形容。

senses.title: Priced above what is fair
senses.definition: charged at a level that is unreasonably high for the good or service
senses.definitionCN: 对商品或服务收取不合理的高价
senses.example: Ten pounds for a cup of tea is plainly excessive.
senses.exampleCN: 一杯茶十英镑，明显贵得过分。
senses.why: A fair price is a boundary set by custom or law, and a price above it has gone beyond.
senses.whyCN: 公道价格是由惯例或法律划出的界线，高出它的价格就是越界。

senses.title: Disproportionate in praise or attention
senses.titleCN: 称赞或关注得不合比例
senses.definition: given more credit, fuss or notice than the thing actually deserves
senses.definitionCN: 给予的赞誉、殷勤或关注超过事物实际应得
senses.example: The young actor received excessive praise for a small part.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻演员只演了一个小角色，却受到过分称赞。
senses.why: Praise has a proper measure too, and passing it turns a compliment into a warning sign.
senses.whyCN: 称赞也有恰当的分量，超过这个分量，赞美就变成警示信号。

senses.title: Beyond the limits of one's authority
senses.definition: exercised beyond the powers that a law, office or contract grants
senses.definitionCN: 行使的权力超出法律、职位或合同所授予的范围
senses.example: The inspector's excessive demands were later ruled unlawful.
senses.exampleCN: 这名检查员越权的要求后来被裁定为不合法。
senses.why: Authority is literally a granted boundary, so official overreach is the clearest legal use of the word.
senses.whyCN: 权限本来就是被授予的边界，因此公务上的越权是这个词最清楚的法律用法。

senses.title: Reacting far too strongly
senses.definition: responding with more anger, fear or emotion than the event justifies
senses.definitionCN: 以超过事件本身应有的愤怒、恐惧或情绪作出回应
senses.example: Her excessive reaction to a small delay surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 她对一次小小的延误反应过激，让所有人都很意外。
senses.why: Emotion is measured against its cause, and a response past that measure has crossed the boundary.
senses.whyCN: 情绪要与其起因相称，超出这个相称度的回应就是越界。

senses.title: A symptom of too much of something
senses.definition: used of a bodily process that occurs more than normal, such as sweating, bleeding or thirst
senses.definitionCN: 用于出汗、出血或口渴等身体过程发生得比正常更多
senses.example: Excessive thirst can be an early sign of diabetes.
senses.exampleCN: 极度口渴可能是糖尿病的早期征兆。
senses.why: Medicine measures every process against a normal range, and readings above it are called excessive.
senses.whyCN: 医学把每种身体过程都与正常范围对照，高于该范围的读数就被称为过度。

senses.title: Overdone in style
senses.definition: using more ornament, emotion or decoration than the subject can carry
senses.definitionCN: 使用的修饰、情感或装饰超过题材所能承载
senses.example: The essay was rejected for its excessive ornament.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章因修饰过度而被退回。
senses.why: Style has a limit set by the subject, and decoration past it buries the meaning instead of serving it.
senses.whyCN: 文风有一条由题材设定的界限，超过它的装饰会埋掉意思，而不是服务意思。

intro.en: Excessive comes from Latin excessus 'a going beyond', from excedere 'to go out, to go beyond', built on ex- 'out' and cedere 'to go, to yield'. French excessif carried it into English in the fifteenth century. The root line is well attested; first dates are approximate.
intro.cn: excessive 出自拉丁 excessus「越界、过度」，源自 excedere「走出去、越过」，由 ex-「出」与 cedere「走、让步」构成。法语 excessif 在十五世纪把它带进英语。词根脉络有据可查；首见年代为约数。

items.en: Cedere meant to go, to withdraw or to yield, and it underlies a large family including accede, proceed and succeed.
items.cn: cedere 意为「走、退让」，是包括 accede、proceed、succeed 在内的庞大词族的底层词根。

items.en: With ex- 'out', excedere meant to go out or to go past a limit, whether of space, number or right.
items.cn: 加上 ex-「出」，excedere 意为走出去或越过界限，无论这界限是空间、数量还是权利。

items.en: The noun excessus named a departure or a going beyond, and it already carried the sense of a breach.
items.cn: 名词 excessus 指离开或越界，本就带有「违规」的意味。

items.en: Old French built the adjective excessif on the Latin noun, and Middle English took it over with the same meaning.
items.cn: 古法语在拉丁名词基础上造出形容词 excessif，中古英语以同一意思接收过来。

items.en: English excessive first described behaviour and spending, then widened to prices, force, medicine and style.
items.cn: 英语的这个词起初描述行为与开支，后来扩展到价格、武力、医学与文风。

items.en: Excessive force, excessive speed and excessive drinking are now legal and medical fixed phrases rather than loose descriptions.
items.cn: 「过度武力」「超速」「酗酒」如今是法律与医学的固定说法，而非随意的描述。

note.en: The first group shares the going-beyond stem; the second group holds words for too much or for extra, each with a different angle.
note.cn: 第一组共享「越界」词干；第二组是表示「过多」或「多余」的词，各有不同角度。

entries.definition: The amount by which something goes beyond a limit; the noun names the surplus, the adjective judges it.
entries.definitionCN: 超出限度的数量；名词指多出来的那部分，形容词对它作评价。

entries.definition: To a degree beyond what is proper; it modifies the action rather than the thing.
entries.definitionCN: 达到超过恰当的程度；修饰动作而非事物。

entries.definition: The quality of being too much; a state noun used in careful or formal prose.
entries.definitionCN: 过分的性质；是状态名词，多用于正式或严谨的文字。

entries.definition: To go beyond a number or limit; the verb states the crossing, the adjective judges the result.
entries.definitionCN: 超过某个数目或限度；动词陈述越界动作，形容词评价结果。

entries.definition: At the farthest end of a scale; it can be neutral or approving, while the target word always disapproves.
entries.definitionCN: 处于尺度的最远端；可中性也可褒义，而目标词总带不赞同。

entries.definition: More than is appropriate, especially in a formal or legal judgement; it stresses unfairness rather than size.
entries.definitionCN: 超过适当程度，多用于正式或法律判断；强调不当，而非数量大。

entries.definition: Left over after needs are met; it is a neutral accounting word and carries no blame.
entries.definitionCN: 需求满足后剩下的；是中性的账目用词，不含责备。

entries.definition: Spending or using far more than one can afford; it adds wastefulness and display.
entries.definitionCN: 花费或使用远超负担能力；多了浪费与炫耀之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means 'out' and the root means 'go': excessive is having gone out past the line.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「出」，词根意为「走」：过度就是走出了那条线。

normal.en: The family runs excess, excessive, excessively and exceed.
normal.cn: 同族词包括过量、过度的、过度地、超过。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the legal side: excessive force, excessive speed.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出法律一面：过度武力、超速。

normal.en: Its opposite is adequate or moderate, both of which stop at the line.
normal.cn: 反义是足够与适度，两者都停在界线之内。

normal.en: The noun excess names the part that spilled over the edge.
normal.cn: 名词 excess 命名溢到边外的那一部分。

abstract.en: Picture a glass filled past the rim while the jug keeps pouring.
abstract.cn: 想象杯子已经满到杯沿，壶还在继续倒。

abstract.en: Picture a thermostat set so high that every window is opened.
abstract.cn: 想象恒温器调得太高，每扇窗都被打开。

abstract.en: Picture a thank-you card so long that the sender forgets the thanks.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长到写的人自己都忘了道谢的感谢卡。

examples.en: Excessive noise from the building site kept the street awake.
examples.cn: 工地过大的噪声让整条街都无法入睡。

examples.en: The judge found the fine excessive for such a minor offence.
examples.cn: 法官认为对如此轻微的过错来说，这笔罚款过高。

examples.en: Doctors warn that excessive salt raises blood pressure.
examples.cn: 医生警告说盐分摄入过量会升高血压。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一筐塞死」——往筐里硬塞到塞死，就是装得过多

root: 拉丁 cedere「走、让步」→ excedere「走出、越过」→ excessus「越界、过度」→ 法语 excessif → 英语 excessive；同族 exceed、excess 共享同一词根。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one movement: crossing a line. The line may be set by need, by law, by a fair price, by authority, by a normal range or by the demands of style.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一个动作：越过一条线。这条线可以由需要、法律、公道价格、权限、正常范围或文体的要求来划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vessel already full, with liquid still being poured over the rim.
core.cn: 核心意象：容器已经满了，液体还在越过边沿往里倒。

branches.en: THE COUNTED SIDE: more units than the purpose needs.
branches.cn: 可计数的一面：数量超过目的所需。

branches.en: THE PRESSURE SIDE: force and emotional reaction past what the case allows.
branches.cn: 压力一面：武力与情绪反应超过情形所允许。

branches.en: THE MARKET SIDE: a charge above a fair level.
branches.cn: 市场一面：收费高于公道水平。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL SIDE: credit and attention beyond what is deserved.
branches.cn: 社交一面：赞誉与关注超过应得。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTIONAL SIDE: overreach of authority, bodily readings above normal, and ornament past the subject's need.
branches.cn: 建制一面：越权、身体读数高于正常，以及超过题材所需的修饰。

intro.en: Excessive joins the Latin prefix ex- 'out', the verb cedere 'go', and the adjective ending -ive; the same root appears in exceed and excess.
intro.cn: excessive 由拉丁前缀 ex-「出」、动词 cedere「走」与形容词词尾 -ive 组成；同一词根也出现在 exceed 与 excess 中。

latinIntro.en: Cedere 'to go' plus ex- 'out' gives excedere 'to go beyond'; its noun excessus gives excess, and the adjective ending -ive gives excessivus, the source of excessive.
latinIntro.cn: cedere「走」加 ex-「出」得出 excedere「越过」；其名词 excessus 给出 excess，加形容词词尾 -ive 得出 excessivus，即 excessive 的来源。

items.example: The prefix marks the crossing of a boundary.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出对边界的越过。

items.example: The verb supplies the motion of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供整个词族的「移动」义。

items.example: The compound verb states the act of overstepping.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词陈述越界的动作。

items.example: The noun already carried a hint of breach.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词本就带有违规的暗示。

items.example: The ending turns the noun into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词变成描述词。

items.example: The adjective always carries disapproval.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词总带不赞同。

items.example: The noun can be neutral in accounting.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词在账目语境中可以中性。

items.example: The verb reports the crossing without judging it.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词只报告越界，不作评价。

items.example: The suffix makes the manner adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成方式副词。

items.example: The suffix names the quality of being too much.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名「过分」的性质。

items.example: The adverb modifies verbs of use and spend.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词修饰「使用」「花费」类动词。

derivatives.zh: 直接来自拉丁 excessus，是该形容词的词基，义为「过量；超额的」
由该形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「过度地」
由该形容词加性质名词后缀构成，义为「过分」
由同一拉丁动词进入英语，义为「超过」

definition_zh: 覆盖广阔的；规模大的；范围广而全面的；影响广泛的；广博的；粗放经营的；外延的；外延量的
definition_en: covering a large area or including a large number of things, rather than being deep or concentrated
core_image: 站在山脊上向下看，草地一直铺到天边，中间没有一道围栏
scene: 雨后站在山脊上，脚下的草地与松林一直铺到天际，中间没有任何围栏。The estate covers an extensive area of moorland and pine.
sceneCN: 这里指覆盖的地域非常广阔（第 1 个义项：所及面积大、铺得很开）；句意为这片庄园覆盖了大片荒原与松林。

pos.zh: 广阔的；广泛的；大规模的

derivatives.zh: 由同一拉丁动词进入英语，义为「延伸；扩展」，是该词族的动作来源
由「延伸」的动词加表示动作结果的名词后缀构成，义为「延伸；扩展部分」
由该形容词加表示方式的副词后缀构成，义为「广泛地；大量地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词后缀构成，义为「广度；广泛性」
由「延伸」的动词加表示「可……的」的形容词后缀构成，义为「可延展的」
由「伸展」的拉丁词干加表示施动者的名词后缀构成，义为「伸肌」

senses.title: Covering a large area
senses.definition: spreading over a wide area of land or surface, measured in space
senses.definitionCN: 在土地或表面上铺开很广，以空间来量度
senses.example: The fire destroyed an extensive stretch of forest.
senses.exampleCN: 大火烧毁了一大片森林。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to stretch out, so the first sense reports how far something has been stretched across the ground.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「向外伸展」，因此第一义说的是某物在地面上铺开了多远。

senses.title: Large in number or scale
senses.definition: involving a large number of items, people or cases rather than a few
senses.definitionCN: 涉及大量项目、人员或案例，而不是少数几个
senses.example: The survey drew on extensive data from forty schools.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查使用了来自四十所学校的大量数据。
senses.why: Counting many units is the numerical form of stretching wide, so the same adjective covers both area and count.
senses.whyCN: 数很多个单位，是「铺得很宽」的数量形式，因此同一个形容词同时覆盖面积与数目。

senses.title: Wide-ranging and thorough
senses.definition: touching on many parts of a subject so that few areas are left out
senses.definitionCN: 涉及一个主题的许多方面，几乎不留空白
senses.example: She has extensive knowledge of medieval trade routes.
senses.exampleCN: 她对中世纪贸易路线有广博的知识。
senses.why: A study that reaches into many corners covers ground, and coverage is the intellectual version of extent.
senses.whyCN: 研究伸进许多角落就是「铺开地面」，而覆盖面正是「广度」在知识上的形态。

senses.title: Affecting a wide range
senses.definition: having effects that reach many places, people or systems
senses.definitionCN: 效果波及许多地方、许多人员或许多系统
senses.example: The storm caused extensive damage along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴在沿海造成了广泛破坏。
senses.why: Damage spreads outward from a centre, and a wide spread is exactly what the root verb describes.
senses.whyCN: 破坏从中心向外扩散，而「大范围扩散」正是这个词根动词所描述的。

senses.title: Broad rather than deep in learning
senses.definition: covering many fields at a general level, often contrasted with specialized depth
senses.definitionCN: 在一般层面上覆盖许多领域，常与专门深度相对
senses.example: His reading is extensive but not very deep.
senses.exampleCN: 他的阅读面很广，但不算深入。
senses.why: The word measures reach, not depth, which is why it can imply breadth without mastery.
senses.whyCN: 这个词量的是「伸到多远」，不是「扎得多深」，因此可以暗示广而不精。

senses.title: Farming across wide land with low input
senses.titleCN: 用广袤土地、低投入耕作
senses.definition: using large areas of land with relatively little labour or capital per hectare
senses.definitionCN: 使用大片土地，每公顷投入的劳动或资本相对很少
senses.example: Extensive farming needs more land than intensive farming.
senses.exampleCN: 粗放耕作比集约耕作需要更多土地。
senses.why: Here the adjective names the strategy of spreading inputs thin across space instead of concentrating them.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个形容词命名的是「把投入摊薄到更大面积」而不是「集中投入」的策略。

senses.title: The range a term applies to
senses.titleCN: 一个词所适用的对象范围
senses.definition: in logic, the set of objects a general term covers, as opposed to its defining content
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑学中一个普遍词项所覆盖的对象集合，与它的定义内涵相对
senses.example: The extensive meaning of the term is wider than its intensive meaning.
senses.exampleCN: 这个术语的外延意义比它的内涵意义更宽。
senses.why: Logic borrowed the spatial word for the spread of cases a term reaches; its partner term is intensive.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学借用了这个空间词，指一个词项所覆盖的个例范围；与之配对的是「内涵」。

senses.title: A quantity that grows with the whole
senses.titleCN: 随整体规模成比例变化的量
senses.definition: in physics, a quantity whose value doubles when the size of the system doubles
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中当系统规模加倍时数值也加倍的量
senses.example: Volume and mass are extensive quantities; temperature is not.
senses.exampleCN: 体积与质量是外延量，温度不是。
senses.why: Such a quantity stretches with the amount of material, while an intensive quantity stays fixed per unit.
senses.whyCN: 这类量随物质多少一起铺开，而强度量则在每一单位上保持不变。

intro.en: Extensive comes from Latin extendere 'to stretch out', built on ex- 'out' and tendere 'to stretch'. Its participle extensus gave the adjective; English took it in the sixteenth century. The root line is clear, though the earliest first-use date is approximate.
intro.cn: extensive 出自拉丁 extendere「向外伸展」，由 ex-「出」与 tendere「伸」构成。其分词 extensus 给出形容词，英语十六世纪引入。词根脉络清楚，最早使用年代为约数。

items.en: Tendere meant to stretch or to draw tight, and it also underlies tension and tendon.
items.cn: tendere 意为伸展或拉紧，也是 tension 与 tendon 的词根。

items.en: With ex- 'out', extendere meant to stretch out or to spread, used of land, hands and time.
items.cn: 加 ex-「出」后，extendere 意为向外伸展、铺开，用于土地、手与时间。

items.en: The participle extensus described something already stretched out, and the adjective grew from it.
items.cn: 分词 extensus 形容已被铺展开的东西，形容词由此而生。

items.en: English extensive first described land and then research, damage and knowledge, keeping the idea of reach.
items.cn: 英语的这个词先形容土地，后形容研究、破坏与知识，始终保留「所及范围」之意。

items.en: Agronomy paired extensive with intensive: broad land and low input against small land and high input.
items.cn: 农学把它与「集约」配对：广土低投入，对应小面积高投入。

items.en: Logic and physics each adopted the pair extensive and intensive, one for range of cases and one for size-dependent quantities.
items.cn: 逻辑学与物理学各自采用「外延」与「内涵」这一对，前者指个例范围，后者指随规模变化的量。

note.en: The first group shares the stretching stem; the second group includes breadth words and its direct opposite.
note.cn: 第一组共享「伸展」词干；第二组包含表示广度的词，以及它的直接对立词。

entries.definition: To stretch something out or to make it longer; the action behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物伸开或加长；是形容词背后的动作。

entries.definition: The act of extending, or a part added; it names the process or the addition.
entries.definitionCN: 延伸的行为，或加上的部分；指过程或附加物。

entries.definition: Over a wide range or in large amounts; it tells how something is done.
entries.definitionCN: 在大范围或大量地；说明做的程度。

entries.definition: The quality of covering much ground; a formal state noun.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖面大的性质；正式的状态名词。

entries.definition: Including everything relevant; it stresses completeness of coverage rather than mere size.
entries.definitionCN: 包含所有相关部分；强调覆盖的完整，而不只是规模大。

entries.definition: Covering many different subjects; it is the plain compound for variety of scope.
entries.definitionCN: 涵盖许多不同主题；是表示范围多样的平实复合词。

entries.definition: Big in size or operation; it measures scale, not the spread of coverage.
entries.definitionCN: 规模或运作上很大；量的是规模，而不是覆盖的铺开程度。

entries.definition: Concentrated on a small area with high input; the direct opposite of broad, low-density use.
entries.definitionCN: 在小面积上集中高投入；与「面积广、投入稀」的用法正相对。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means 'out' and the root means 'stretch': extensive is stretched far and wide.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「出」，词根意为「伸」：广就是向四面八方伸出去。

normal.en: The family runs extend, extension, extensively and extensible.
normal.cn: 同族词包括延伸、扩展、广泛地、可延展的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the area side: extensive damage, extensive forest.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出面积一面：大面积破坏、广阔森林。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the study side: extensive research, extensive reading.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出研究一面：广泛研究、泛读。

normal.en: Its built-in partner is intensive, which measures concentration instead of reach.
normal.cn: 它的固定搭档是 intensive，量的是集中度而不是所及范围。

abstract.en: Picture a single fence line so long that it disappears behind a hill.
abstract.cn: 想象一道围栏长到在山后消失。

abstract.en: Picture one bookcase that holds a little of every subject.
abstract.cn: 想象一个书架，每门学科都只放一点。

abstract.en: Picture a field dotted with one shepherd per hundred hectares.
abstract.cn: 想象一片田野，每百公顷才有一个牧人。

examples.en: The museum owns an extensive collection of ancient coins.
examples.cn: 这座博物馆藏有大量古钱币。

examples.en: Extensive repairs kept the bridge closed all summer.
examples.cn: 大规模的维修让这座桥整个夏天关闭。

examples.en: Extensive farming leaves part of the land unused each year.
examples.cn: 粗放耕作每年都会让一部分土地闲置。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一筐伸出去」——一筐东西向四面伸得很远，就是广泛铺开

root: 拉丁 tendere「伸、拉紧」→ extendere「向外伸展」→ 分词 extensus → 英语 extensive；同族 extend、extension、tension。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: stretching outward. What stretches may be land, a data set, a field of study, damage, farmland, the reach of a term, or a physical quantity.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个动作：向外伸展。伸展的可以是土地、数据集、研究领域、破坏范围、农田、术语所及的对象，也可以是某个物理量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something stretched outward until it reaches far across the ground, with depth left thin.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物向外伸展，直到在地面上铺得很远，而厚度保持很薄。

branches.en: THE SPATIAL BASE: a wide area of ground or surface.
branches.cn: 空间基础：大片土地或表面。

branches.en: THE COUNTED FORM: many items rather than a few.
branches.cn: 计数形式：项目多而非少数。

branches.en: THE INTELLECTUAL FORM: wide coverage of a field, and breadth without depth.
branches.cn: 知识形式：覆盖领域广，以及广而不深。

branches.en: THE OUTWARD EFFECT: damage or change reaching many places.
branches.cn: 向外效果：破坏或变化波及多处。

branches.en: THE TECHNICAL USES: low-input farming over wide land, the range of a term, and a size-dependent quantity.
branches.cn: 专业用法：广土低投入的耕作、术语所及范围，以及随规模变化的量。

intro.en: Extensive is built from Latin ex- 'out', tendere 'to stretch', the participle ending, and the adjective ending -ive.
intro.cn: extensive 由拉丁 ex-「出」、tendere「伸」、分词词尾与形容词词尾 -ive 构成。

latinIntro.en: Tendere gives extensus, whose stem plus -ive gives extensivus, the source of English extensive.
latinIntro.cn: tendere 给出 extensus，其词干加 -ive 得出 extensivus，即英语 extensive 的来源。

items.example: The prefix points the stretching outward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把伸展指向外。

items.example: The verb supplies the motion of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供整个词族的动作。

items.example: The compound verb names the spreading.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词命名铺开的动作。

items.example: The participle became the adjective base.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词成为形容词的基础。

items.example: The ending makes a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成描述词。

items.example: English added the sense of large scale.
items.exampleCN: 英语加上了「规模大」的意思。

items.example: The verb states the action plainly.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词平实地陈述动作。

items.meaning: a stretching or an added part
items.example: The noun names the process or its result.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名过程或结果。

items.example: The suffix makes the manner adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成方式副词。

items.example: The suffix names the quality of breadth.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名「广度」这一性质。

由「延伸」加动作名词后缀构成，义为「扩展部分」
由该形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「广泛地」
由该形容词加性质名词后缀构成，义为「广度」
