definition_zh: 完全相同的；同一个的；同卵双生的；一模一样的复制品；恒等的；基因相同的；前后一致的；全等的
definition_en: exactly the same in every detail, or being one and the same thing
core_image: 检验台上并排放着两只杯子，连杯沿同一处的细小缺口都落在一样的位置
scene: 工厂的检验台上并排放着两只杯子，连杯沿同一处的细小缺口都落在一样的位置。The two vases are identical down to a tiny chip on the rim.
sceneCN: 这里指各处细节完全一样、找不出差别（第 1 个义项：细节上毫无差异）；句意为这两只花瓶连杯沿一处小缺口都完全相同。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁 identitas「同一性」直接进入英语，义为「身份；同一性」，是该词族的抽象名词
由该形容词加表示方式的副词后缀构成，义为「完全相同地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词后缀构成，义为「完全相同」
由同一「同一」词根加表示「使……化」的动词后缀构成，义为「辨认；确认身份」
由「辨认」的动词加表示动作结果的名词后缀构成，义为「辨认；身份证明」
由该动词加表示工具或施动者的名词后缀构成，义为「标识符」

senses.title: Exactly alike in every detail
senses.definition: so alike that no difference can be found between two separate things
senses.definitionCN: 两个独立事物相像到找不出任何差别
senses.example: The two reports are identical in wording.
senses.exampleCN: 这两份报告在措辞上一模一样。
senses.why: The Latin root is the word for 'the same', so the first sense simply says that two things match completely.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根就是「同一个」这个词，因此第一义只是说两件事完全吻合。

senses.title: One and the same thing
senses.definition: being numerically one object referred to twice, rather than two objects that resemble each other
senses.definitionCN: 指同一个对象被提到两次，而不是两个彼此相像的对象
senses.example: The witness and the accused were identical, though nobody knew it.
senses.exampleCN: 证人与被告本是同一个人，只是没人知道。
senses.why: Identity in philosophy means oneness, not resemblance, and English keeps that stricter sense alongside the looser one.
senses.whyCN: 哲学上的同一性指「是一个」，不是「像」，英语把这个更严格的意思与较宽松的意思并存保留。

senses.title: Developed from one fertilized egg
senses.titleCN: 由同一个受精卵发育而来
senses.definition: said of twins that come from a single egg and therefore share the same genes
senses.definitionCN: 用于由单一受精卵发育、因而共享同一套基因的双胞胎
senses.example: Identical twins often differ in personality despite their genes.
senses.exampleCN: 同卵双胞胎尽管基因相同，性格却常常不同。
senses.why: Their starting material is literally one, so the word for sameness names the biological origin rather than appearance.
senses.whyCN: 他们的起点材料字面上就是一个，因此这个表示「同一」的词命名的是生物来源，而不是外貌。

senses.title: A copy with no difference
senses.definition: a duplicate made to match an original exactly, so that the two cannot be told apart
senses.definitionCN: 按原件精确制作、无法与原件区分的复制品
senses.example: The museum displayed an identical copy beside the original.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆把一件一模一样的复制品摆在原件旁边。
senses.why: A faithful copy reaches the limit of likeness, which is exactly the boundary the adjective marks.
senses.whyCN: 忠实的复制品达到了相似的极限，而这正是这个形容词所划的界线。

senses.title: True for every value, in algebra
senses.titleCN: 代数中对一切取值都成立的
senses.definition: said of an equation that holds for all values of its variables, unlike a conditional equation
senses.definitionCN: 用于对所有变量取值都成立的方程，与条件方程相对
senses.example: The teacher asked why the identical equation needs no solution step.
senses.exampleCN: 老师问为什么恒等式不需要求解步骤。
senses.why: Both sides are the same expression throughout, so the equation is 'identical' in the literal sense.
senses.whyCN: 等式两边始终是同一个表达式，因此这个方程在字面意义上就是「同一个」。

senses.title: Carrying the same genes
senses.definition: having an identical genetic makeup, as clones or laboratory strains do
senses.definitionCN: 具有完全相同的基因组成，如克隆体或实验品系
senses.example: The lab keeps identical mice to control for variation.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室饲养基因相同的小鼠以控制变量。
senses.why: Experimental control requires sameness of material, and the word states that sameness at the genetic level.
senses.whyCN: 实验控制要求材料相同，这个词就把这种相同说到基因层面。

senses.title: Agreeing word for word
senses.definition: matching another account, version or record so closely that no discrepancy appears
senses.definitionCN: 与另一份陈述、版本或记录贴得极近，看不出出入
senses.example: Both witnesses gave identical accounts of the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 两位证人对事故的描述完全一致。
senses.why: Two statements can be compared detail by detail, and full agreement is likeness taken to the limit.
senses.whyCN: 两份陈述可以逐条比对，完全吻合就是把相似推到极限。

senses.title: Coinciding exactly in geometry
senses.definition: said of figures that can be superimposed so that every point matches
senses.definitionCN: 用于能够完全叠合、每一点都吻合的图形
senses.example: The two triangles are identical in shape and size.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个三角形在形状与大小上完全相同。
senses.why: Geometry tests sameness by moving one figure onto another, and perfect overlap is the strictest test.
senses.whyCN: 几何用把一个图形移到另一个上的办法检验相同，完全重合是最严格的检验。

intro.en: Identical comes from Medieval Latin identicus, built on Late Latin identitas 'sameness', from Latin idem 'the same'. English took the adjective in the seventeenth century. The chain is well attested; only first dates are approximate.
intro.cn: identical 来自中世纪拉丁 identicus，建立在晚期拉丁 identitas「同一性」之上，后者源于拉丁 idem「同一个」。英语十七世纪引入这个形容词。构词链有据可查，只有首见年代为约数。

items.en: Idem meant 'the same', used in citation and argument to point back to one thing already named.
items.cn: idem 意为「同一个」，在引用与论证中用来回指已经提到的同一事物。

items.en: Late Latin identitas named sameness or oneness, formed irregularly from idem rather than from a standard stem.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 identitas 指同一或单一，由 idem 不规则地构成，而非取自标准词干。

items.en: Scholastic Latin built identicus for 'the same in substance', a word used in theology and logic.
items.cn: 经院拉丁造出 identicus，表示「实质相同」，用于神学与逻辑。

items.en: English adopted identical for things that agree in every respect, and set it beside the older noun identity.
items.cn: 英语采用这个词表示各方面都一致的事物，并与更早的名词 identity 并置。

items.en: Twins, fingerprints and later clones gave the word concrete uses where sameness could be tested.
items.cn: 双胞胎、指纹以及后来的克隆给这个词带来可检验「相同」的具体用法。

items.en: Algebra distinguishes an identical equation, true for all values, from one solved for particular values.
items.cn: 代数把对一切取值都成立的恒等式，与只对特定取值求解的方程区分开来。

note.en: The first group shares the same root; the second group holds words for likeness, each allowing a different degree.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一词根；第二组是表示相似的词，各自允许的程度不同。

entries.definition: The state of being the same, or who a person is; the noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 同一的状态，或一个人的身份；是形容词背后的名词。

entries.definition: In exactly the same way; it compares two actions or arrangements.
entries.definitionCN: 以完全相同的方式；比较两个动作或安排。

entries.definition: To recognize or establish who or what something is; it acts on identity rather than likeness.
entries.definitionCN: 认出或确定某人某物是什么；作用于「身份」而非「相似」。

entries.definition: The act of recognizing, or the document that proves who one is.
entries.definitionCN: 辨认的行为，或证明身份的文件。

entries.definition: The plain word for oneness or likeness; it can mean either, while the target word insists on exactness.
entries.definitionCN: 表示同一或相似的平实词；两种都可指，而目标词坚持「精确相同」。

entries.definition: Similar in appearance; it is weaker and normally used after the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 外貌相似；程度更弱，通常作表语。

entries.definition: Equal in value, function or meaning; it permits different forms that do the same job.
entries.definitionCN: 在价值、功能或意义上相等；允许形式不同但作用相同。

entries.definition: Impossible to tell apart by the senses; it reports a limit of perception rather than proven sameness.
entries.definitionCN: 感官上无法区分；说的是感知的极限，而非已被证明的相同。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root is Latin for 'the same', so identity and identical are one family.
normal.cn: 词根就是拉丁语的「同一个」，因此身份与完全相同属于同一族。

normal.en: The family runs identical, identically, identity, identify and identification.
normal.cn: 同族词包括目标词、相同地、身份、辨认、身份证明。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the copy side: identical copy, identical to.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出复制一面：一模一样的副本、与……完全相同。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark biology and maths: identical twins, identical equation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出生物与数学：同卵双胞胎、恒等式。

normal.en: It takes more and most: more identical sounds odd but is standard in careful comparison.
normal.cn: 比较级用 more、最高级用 most，在严谨比较中虽略显拗口却是标准形式。

abstract.en: Picture two keys cut from one pattern, each opening the same lock.
abstract.cn: 想象两把按同一模板切出的钥匙，都能开同一把锁。

abstract.en: Picture two pages of text held to the light, line for line aligned.
abstract.cn: 想象两页文字对着光，一行一行都能对齐。

abstract.en: Picture one face reflected in two mirrors at once.
abstract.cn: 想象同一张脸同时映在两面镜子里。

examples.en: The two samples were identical under the microscope.
examples.cn: 这两个样本在显微镜下完全相同。

examples.en: Her second answer was identical to her first.
examples.cn: 她的第二次回答与第一次一字不差。

examples.en: Identical twins do not always share the same illnesses.
examples.cn: 同卵双胞胎并不总是得同样的病。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱等提扣」——两个人像到连提的扣子都一样，就是完全相同

root: 拉丁 idem「同一个」→ 晚期拉丁 identitas「同一性」→ 中世纪拉丁 identicus「实质相同的」→ 英语 identical；同族 identity、identify。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses push one idea to its limit: the same. It can be the same details, the same object, the same genes, the same wording or a figure that overlaps exactly.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一个观念推到极限：相同。可以是细节相同、对象同一、基因相同、字句相同，也可以是图形完全重合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two objects laid side by side with no visible difference anywhere.
core.cn: 核心意象：两件东西并排放着，任何地方都看不出差别。

branches.en: THE GENERAL TEST: no difference can be found between two things.
branches.cn: 一般检验：两件东西之间找不出差别。

branches.en: THE STRICT TEST: one object, mentioned twice.
branches.cn: 严格检验：同一个对象被提到两次。

branches.en: THE BIOLOGICAL FORM: twins from one egg, and organisms with the same genes.
branches.cn: 生物形态：同一受精卵的双胞胎，以及基因相同的生物。

branches.en: THE REPEATED FORM: an exact duplicate, and two accounts that agree word for word.
branches.cn: 重复形态：精确的复制品，以及字句一致的两份陈述。

branches.en: THE FORMAL FORM: an equation true for all values, and figures that coincide point for point.
branches.cn: 形式化形态：对一切取值成立的方程，以及点点重合的图形。

intro.en: Identical is built on Latin idem 'the same', the state noun identitas, and the adjective ending -al.
intro.cn: identical 建立在拉丁 idem「同一个」、状态名词 identitas 与形容词词尾 -al 之上。

latinIntro.en: Idem gives identitas irregularly; Medieval Latin identicus adds the adjective ending, and English adapts it as identical.
latinIntro.cn: idem 不规则地给出 identitas；中世纪拉丁 identicus 加上形容词词尾，英语把它改造为 identical。

items.example: The pronoun points back to one thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个代词回指同一事物。

items.example: The suffix names the state of sameness.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾命名「相同」的状态。

items.example: The noun formed irregularly from the pronoun.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词由代词不规则构成。

items.example: Scholastic Latin used it in argument.
items.exampleCN: 经院拉丁把它用于论证。

items.example: The ending turns the medieval word into an English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把中世纪拉丁词变成英语形容词。

items.example: English narrowed it to exact sameness.
items.exampleCN: 英语把它收窄为「精确相同」。

items.example: The noun kept both the logical and personal senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词同时保留逻辑与个人两义。

items.example: The suffix gives the adverb of manner.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀给出方式副词。

items.example: The verb acts on who or what a thing is.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词作用于事物的身份。

items.example: The suffix names the quality of exact likeness.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名「精确相同」的性质。

definition_zh: 立即的；直接的；紧邻的；直系的；当前的；直觉的；最紧迫的；即期的
definition_en: happening at once, or coming directly without anything in between
core_image: 火警铃刚响，车间里的人已经放下手上的活，转身朝门口走
scene: 火警铃一响，车间里的人立刻放下手上的活，转身朝门口走。The alarm brought an immediate halt to the production line.
sceneCN: 这里指事情在下一刻就发生、没有等待（第 1 个义项：紧接着、毫不延迟）；句意为警报让生产线立刻停了下来。

collocations.zh: 立即生效；立竿见影的效果

由该形容词的词干加表示性质的名词后缀构成，义为「直接性；紧迫感」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词后缀构成，义为「直接；无中介」
由同一「中间」词根加动词词尾构成，义为「调解；居中传递」，与目标词共享「处于中间」的词根

senses.title: Happening at once
senses.definition: following something with no delay or waiting period
senses.definitionCN: 紧随某事发生，没有延迟或等待
senses.example: The medicine gave immediate relief.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药立刻缓解了症状。
senses.why: If nothing stands between cause and result, the gap in time disappears, and the word for 'no interval' means 'at once'.
senses.whyCN: 若原因与结果之间不隔任何东西，时间上的间隔也就消失，于是「无间隔」的词就表示「立刻」。

senses.title: Direct, with nothing in between
senses.definition: acting as the first link in a chain, with no intermediate step or agent
senses.definitionCN: 作为链条上的第一环，中间没有过渡步骤或中间人
senses.example: Smoking was the immediate cause of the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 吸烟是这场火灾的直接原因。
senses.why: The prefix denies an intervening middle, so a cause that touches its effect directly is called immediate.
senses.whyCN: 前缀否定「中间介入」，因此直接触及其结果的原因就被称为直接的。

senses.title: Nearest in space
senses.definition: closest to a place or person, with no other object between
senses.definitionCN: 离某地或某人最近，中间没有别的东西
senses.example: Only the immediate vicinity of the station was evacuated.
senses.exampleCN: 只疏散了车站紧邻的区域。
senses.why: Distance is measured as a series of gaps, and zero gaps gives the nearest ring around a point.
senses.whyCN: 距离被看作一串间隔，间隔为零就得到围绕某点的最近一圈。

senses.title: Closest by family relation
senses.definition: said of the closest relatives, such as parents, children and siblings
senses.definitionCN: 用于最亲近的亲属，如父母、子女与兄弟姐妹
senses.example: Only immediate family were told the news first.
senses.exampleCN: 消息最先只告诉了直系亲属。
senses.why: Family lines can be drawn with branches or without, and the unbranched line is the immediate one.
senses.whyCN: 亲属关系可画成有旁支或没有旁支的线，没有旁支的那条线就是「直系」。

senses.title: The period right ahead
senses.definition: belonging to the present or the very near future, as opposed to the long term
senses.definitionCN: 属于当下或极近的将来，与长期相对
senses.example: Our immediate task is to find shelter before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 我们眼下的任务是在天黑前找到落脚处。
senses.why: Time is pictured as a line of intervals, and the one that touches the present is the immediate one.
senses.whyCN: 时间被想象成一串间隔，与当下相接的那一段就是「直接的」。

senses.title: Felt before any reasoning
senses.definition: experienced directly through the senses or feelings, before thought or interpretation
senses.definitionCN: 通过感官或感受直接体验，先于思考或解释
senses.example: Her immediate impression was that the room was too cold.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第一直觉是这间屋子太冷。
senses.why: An impression with no reasoning between event and feeling is described in the same way as a direct cause.
senses.whyCN: 事件与感受之间不隔推理，这样的印象就与直接原因用了同一种说法。

senses.title: Most pressing right now
senses.definition: demanding attention before anything else, because delay would cause harm
senses.definitionCN: 要求先于其他一切得到处理，因为拖延会造成损害
senses.example: The leaking roof is our immediate concern.
senses.exampleCN: 漏雨的屋顶是我们眼下最要紧的事。
senses.why: What cannot wait is what sits closest in time, so priority is expressed as immediacy.
senses.whyCN: 等不得的事在时间上离得最近，因此优先事项就用「无间隔」来表达。

senses.title: Due at once in trade or law
senses.definition: payable or effective at once, said of payment, delivery or possession
senses.definitionCN: 立即应付或生效，用于付款、交付或占有
senses.example: The contract requires immediate payment on delivery.
senses.exampleCN: 合同要求货到即付。
senses.why: Commerce sets dates for performance, and a date that is today rather than later is immediate.
senses.whyCN: 商业为履行设定日期，定在今天而不是以后的日期就是「即期」。

intro.en: Immediate is Latin immediatus, from in- 'not' plus mediatus 'intervening', the participle of mediare 'to be in the middle', from medius 'middle'. English took it in the fifteenth century. The formation is clear; first dates are approximate.
intro.cn: immediate 来自拉丁 immediatus，由 in-「不」与 mediatus「居间介入的」构成，后者是 mediare「处于中间」的分词，而 medius 意为「中间」。英语十五世纪引入。构词清楚，首见年代为约数。

items.en: Medius meant middle or in the middle, and it underlies medium, median and intermediate.
items.cn: medius 意为中间或在中间，是 medium、median、intermediate 的词根。

items.en: The verb mediare meant to be in the middle or to act as a go-between, hence English mediate.
items.cn: 动词 mediare 意为处于中间或充当中介，由此产生英语的 mediate。

items.en: Its participle mediatus described something that has been interposed between two parties.
items.cn: 其分词 mediatus 描述被插在两方之间的东西。

items.en: With in- 'not', immediatus meant having nothing interposed, whether in space, time or causation.
items.cn: 加上 in-「不」，immediatus 意为不隔任何东西，无论空间、时间还是因果。

items.en: English immediate first described direct contact and direct causes, then extended to time and kinship.
items.cn: 英语的这个词先描述直接接触与直接原因，随后扩展到时间与亲属关系。

items.en: Immediate payment, immediate delivery and immediate possession are fixed phrases where the date is today.
items.cn: 「即期付款」「立即交付」「即时占有」都是把日期定在今天的固定说法。

note.en: The first group shares the middle root; the second group holds words for speed and directness, each with a different centre.
note.cn: 第一组共享「中间」词根；第二组是表示迅速与直接的词，各自的侧重不同。

entries.definition: At once, or directly; also used of place, as 'immediately behind'.
entries.definitionCN: 立刻，或直接地；也可用于位置，如「紧挨着后面」。

entries.definition: The quality of being direct and unmediated, or of feeling urgent.
entries.definitionCN: 直接、不经中介的性质，或紧迫感。

entries.definition: To stand between parties and help them agree; the root verb that the prefix denies.
entries.definitionCN: 站在两方之间帮他们达成一致；正是被前缀否定的那个词根动词。

entries.definition: Sitting between two levels; it keeps the middle, where the target word removes it.
entries.definitionCN: 位于两个层级之间；保留了「中间」，而目标词把中间去掉。

entries.definition: Happening in an extremely short moment; it measures time almost as zero, not absence of an intermediary.
entries.definitionCN: 在极短瞬间发生；把时间量到近乎零，而不是强调无中介。

entries.definition: Without anyone or anything in between; it is close, but applies mainly to routes, contact and causes.
entries.definitionCN: 中间不经任何人或物；意思接近，但主要用于路线、接触与原因。

entries.definition: Needing attention now; it stresses the pressure to act rather than the absence of a gap.
entries.definitionCN: 需要现在就处理；强调行动压力，而不是没有间隔。

entries.definition: Nearest or most direct, used in formal analysis of causes; it is the technical cousin of the target word.
entries.definitionCN: 最近的或最直接的，用于正式的因果分析；是目标词的技术性近亲。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix says 'not' and the root says 'middle': immediate means no middle at all.
normal.cn: 前缀是「不」，词根是「中间」：直接就是完全没有中间。

normal.en: The family runs immediately, immediacy, mediate and intermediate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括立即、直接性、调解、中间的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark time: immediate effect, immediate action, immediate future.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出时间：立即生效、立即行动、最近的将来。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark closeness: immediate vicinity, immediate family.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出贴近：紧邻地区、直系亲属。

normal.en: In commerce it fixes today as the date: immediate payment, immediate delivery.
normal.cn: 商业中它把今天定为日期：即期付款、立即交付。

abstract.en: Picture a hand touching a switch with no glove in between.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手直接按上开关，中间没有手套。

abstract.en: Picture a phone ringing in the same second as a message arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象消息到达的同一秒电话就响了。

abstract.en: Picture standing at the edge of a station platform, one step from the door.
abstract.cn: 想象站在站台边，离车门只有一步。

examples.en: The new rule had an immediate effect on traffic.
examples.cn: 新规定对交通立刻产生了效果。

examples.en: Nobody in her immediate family had heard of the plan.
examples.cn: 她的直系亲属中没人听说过这个计划。

examples.en: His immediate reaction was to cover the child with his coat.
examples.cn: 他的第一反应是用外套护住孩子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一眯地」——眼睛一眯的工夫就到了，形容立刻、不隔片刻

root: 拉丁 medius「中间」→ mediare「处于中间」→ 分词 mediatus「居间的」→ 加 in-「不」得 immediatus → 英语 immediate。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all deny a gap. What is removed may be a delay, an intermediate cause, a distance, a generation, a stretch of time, a step of reasoning or a payment date.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在否定一个间隔。被去掉的可以是延迟、中间原因、距离、一代人、一段时间、一步推理，或一个付款日期。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two things touching, with nothing placed between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：两样东西贴在一起，中间没有放任何东西。

branches.en: THE TIME GAP REMOVED: the result arrives at once.
branches.cn: 时间间隔被去掉：结果立刻到来。

branches.en: THE CAUSAL GAP REMOVED: the first link is the direct cause.
branches.cn: 因果间隔被去掉：第一环就是直接原因。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL GAP REMOVED: the nearest place, and the closest kin.
branches.cn: 关系间隔被去掉：最近的地带与最亲的亲属。

branches.en: THE TIME HORIZON: the period touching now, and what must be handled before anything else.
branches.cn: 时间视野：与当下相接的时段，以及必须先处理的事。

branches.en: THE UNMEDIATED REMAINDER: feeling before thought, and a date fixed at today.
branches.cn: 其余的无中介情形：先于思考的感受，以及定在今天的日期。

intro.en: Immediate is the Latin negative prefix in- plus the participle of mediare 'to be in the middle', itself from medius 'middle'.
intro.cn: immediate 是拉丁否定前缀 in- 加上 mediare「处于中间」的分词，而后者源于 medius「中间」。

latinIntro.en: Medius 'middle' gives mediare 'to be in the middle'; its participle mediatus with in- 'not' gives immediatus, the source of the English adjective.
latinIntro.cn: medius「中间」给出 mediare「处于中间」；其分词 mediatus 加 in-「不」得出 immediatus，即英语形容词的来源。

items.example: The prefix denies any middle term.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀否定任何中间项。

items.example: The adjective is the root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是整个词族的根。

items.example: The verb also gives English mediate.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词也给出英语的 mediate。

items.example: The participle names what stands between.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词命名「立在中间的东西」。

items.example: The compound covers space, time and cause.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词覆盖空间、时间与因果。

items.example: The ending appears in both immediate and mediate.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾同时出现在目标词与 mediate 中。

items.example: English extended it to kinship and trade.
items.exampleCN: 英语把它扩展到亲属与商业。

items.example: The adverb covers both time and place.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词同时覆盖时间与位置。

items.example: The suffix gives immediacy, the quality of being direct.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀给出「直接性」这一性质。

items.example: The unprefixed verb keeps the middle.
items.exampleCN: 不带前缀的动词保留了「中间」。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「立即地」
由该形容词词干加性质名词后缀构成，义为「直接性」
由该形容词加性质名词后缀构成，义为「无中介」
由同一「中间」词根构成，义为「调解」

definition_zh: 固有的；与生俱来的；字里隐含的；无法分离的；法律上固有的；材料本身具有的；逻辑上内含的；生物固有的
definition_en: existing as a natural and permanent part of something, so that it cannot be separated from it
core_image: 老屋墙脚总是渗着湿气，刷多少层漆都盖不住，湿气像是从石头里长出来的
scene: 老屋的墙脚总是渗着湿气，刷多少层漆都盖不住，那湿气像是从石头里长出来的。Old stone walls have an inherent dampness that no paint can hide.
sceneCN: 这里指事物本身固有、靠外力去不掉的（第 1 个义项：作为某物天然组成部分而存在）；句意为老石墙自带一种漆也盖不住的潮气。

pos.zh: 固有的；内在的；与生俱来的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示方式的副词后缀构成，义为「固有地；本质上」
由该形容词的词干加表示状态的名词后缀构成，义为「固有；内在性」
由同一词干加另一表示性质的名词后缀构成，义为「固有性」，多用于哲学与法律
由拉丁 inhaerere 直接进入英语，义为「固有于；存在于」，是该词族的动词
同词根加表示「朝向」的前缀构成，义为「附着的；拥护者」，与目标词共享「粘住」的词根

senses.title: Existing as a natural part
senses.titleCN: 作为天然组成部分而存在
senses.definition: belonging to something so completely that it cannot be taken away without changing the thing
senses.definitionCN: 完全属于某物，取走就会改变该物，因而无法去除
senses.example: Every alloy has inherent limits on how far it can bend.
senses.exampleCN: 每种合金在弯曲程度上都有固有的极限。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to stick fast inside, so the adjective pictures a quality lodged in the material itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「牢牢粘在里面」，因此这个形容词画出一种卡在材料内部的素质。

senses.title: Present from birth in a person
senses.definition: part of a person's nature from birth rather than acquired by training
senses.definitionCN: 自出生起就是某人天性的一部分，而非训练所得
senses.example: She has an inherent sense of rhythm that lessons only refined.
senses.exampleCN: 她有一种与生俱来的节奏感，课程只是把它打磨得更细。
senses.why: What is stuck in a person from the start cannot be attributed to later learning.
senses.whyCN: 从一开始就「粘」在人身上的东西，不能归因于后来的学习。

senses.title: Implied in the meaning of words
senses.definition: contained in the meaning of a term even when it is not stated openly
senses.definitionCN: 即使没有明说，也包含在一个词项的意义之中
senses.example: The word 'alone' carries an inherent suggestion of sadness.
senses.exampleCN: 「独自」这个词本身就隐含一丝悲凉。
senses.why: A meaning can hold another meaning inside it, the same way a substance holds a quality.
senses.whyCN: 一个意义可以把另一个意义包在里面，正如一种物质含有某种性质。

senses.title: A risk that cannot be separated
senses.definition: a danger or weakness built into an activity so that avoiding it would mean abandoning the activity
senses.definitionCN: 活动本身带来的危险或缺陷，避开它就等于放弃这项活动
senses.example: Some risk is inherent in any surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 任何手术都存在某种固有风险。
senses.why: If the risk comes attached to the practice, no amount of care removes it entirely.
senses.whyCN: 若风险随这项实践一同附着而来，再小心也无法彻底去掉它。

senses.title: A right that belongs by office
senses.titleCN: 因职位本身而有的权利
senses.definition: a power or right held because of the nature of an office or a legal position
senses.definitionCN: 因职位或法律地位的性质而拥有的权力或权利
senses.example: The court has an inherent power to control its own process.
senses.exampleCN: 法院拥有管理自身程序的固有权力。
senses.why: Legal English treats certain powers as attached to the office rather than granted by a separate document.
senses.whyCN: 法律英语把某些权力看作附着于职位本身，而不是由另一份文件授予。

senses.title: A property of the material itself
senses.definition: a physical property that comes from the substance, not from how it is shaped or used
senses.definitionCN: 由物质本身而来的物理性质，而非由形状或用途造成
senses.example: Rust resistance is inherent in stainless steel.
senses.exampleCN: 抗锈性是不锈钢本身固有的。
senses.why: Testing separates what the substance brings from what the process adds, and the former is inherent.
senses.whyCN: 检测要把物质自带的与工艺添加的区分开，前者就是固有的。

senses.title: A contradiction contained within
senses.definition: a conflict that follows from the very definition of a system, so it cannot be removed by adjustment
senses.definitionCN: 由体系定义本身推出的冲突，无法靠调整消除
senses.example: Critics point to an inherent contradiction in the policy.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者指出这项政策存在内在矛盾。
senses.why: Logic can hold one statement inside another, and a conflict so held is inherent rather than accidental.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑可以把一个陈述包在另一个里，这样被包住的冲突就是内在的，而非偶然的。

senses.title: Defence present from the start
senses.definition: said of biological protection that an organism is born with, as opposed to acquired immunity
senses.definitionCN: 用于生物体天生具备的保护，与后天获得的免疫相对
senses.example: Inherent immunity blocks many bacteria before antibodies form.
senses.exampleCN: 在抗体形成之前，固有免疫就已挡住许多细菌。
senses.why: The body's first line is already in place, so medicine calls it inherent rather than learned.
senses.whyCN: 身体的第一道防线早已就位，因此医学称它为固有的，而不是后天学来的。

intro.en: Inherent comes from Latin inhaerere 'to stick in', built on in- 'in' and haerere 'to stick, to cling'. Its participle inhaerens gave the adjective, which English took in the seventeenth century. The same root yields adhere and hesitate.
intro.cn: inherent 来自拉丁 inhaerere「粘在里面」，由 in-「在内」与 haerere「粘住」构成。其分词 inhaerens 给出形容词，英语十七世纪引入。同一词根还产生 adhere 与 hesitate。

items.en: Haerere meant to stick, to cling or to be stuck fast, and it could describe both glue and a stalled mind.
items.cn: haerere 意为粘住、附着或卡住不动，既能形容胶，也能形容卡住的思路。

items.en: With in- 'in', inhaerere meant to stick inside something, and it described qualities that cling to a subject.
items.cn: 加 in-「在内」，inhaerere 意为粘在内部，用来描述附着于主体的性质。

items.en: The participle inhaerens named what inheres, and philosophy used it for properties that belong to a substance.
items.cn: 分词 inhaerens 命名「内居的东西」，哲学用它指属于实体的属性。

items.en: English adopted the adjective in theology and natural philosophy before it became an everyday word.
items.cn: 英语在神学与自然哲学中先采用这个形容词，之后才成为日常用词。

items.en: Law uses inherent for powers and rights attached to an office, not created by a separate grant.
items.cn: 法律用这个词指附着于职位的权力与权利，而非由另一次授予创造。

items.en: Inherent stresses the attachment to a subject; intrinsic stresses what lies within a thing's own nature, apart from anything external.
items.cn: inherent 强调「附着于主体」；intrinsic 强调「属于事物自身本质内部、与外来因素无关」。

note.en: The first group shares the clinging stem; the second group holds the words most often confused with it.
note.cn: 第一组共享「粘住」词干；第二组列出最容易被它与混淆的几个词。

entries.definition: To exist as a permanent quality in something; the verb behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 作为永久性质存在于某物之中；是形容词背后的动词。

entries.definition: The state of existing inside something as a quality; a formal philosophical noun.
entries.definitionCN: 作为性质存在于某物内部的状态；正式的哲学名词。

entries.definition: By its own nature; it marks a judgement about what cannot be changed.
entries.definitionCN: 就其本性而言；标出「无法改变」这一判断。

entries.definition: Sticking to a surface, or a person who supports a cause; it adds the idea of attaching from outside.
entries.definitionCN: 附着在表面上，或指拥护某个主张的人；多了「从外部贴上」之意。

entries.definition: Belonging to a thing's own inner nature, measured without reference to anything outside; it stresses the inside rather than the attachment.
entries.definitionCN: 属于事物自身的内在本质，不参照外部来量度；强调「内部」而非「附着」。

entries.definition: Present from birth, used mainly of living things and abilities; it marks origin in time rather than inseparability.
entries.definitionCN: 出生时即有，主要用于生物与能力；标出时间上的来源，而非不可分离。

entries.definition: Belonging to the essence, so that without it the thing would not be what it is; stronger than mere attachment.
entries.definitionCN: 属于本质，缺了它事物就不成其为该物；比单纯「附着」更强。

entries.definition: Included as part of a product's design; the everyday compound for qualities installed rather than grown.
entries.definitionCN: 作为产品设计的一部分内置；是日常复合词，指装进去而非长出来的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means 'in' and the root means 'stick': inherent is stuck inside and will not come out.
normal.cn: 前缀是「在内」，词根是「粘」：固有的就是粘在里面取不出来。

normal.en: The family runs inhere, inherence, inherently and adherent.
normal.cn: 同族词包括固有、固有性、固有地、附着的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark risk and defect: inherent risk, inherent weakness.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出风险与缺陷：固有风险、内在缺陷。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark law and logic: inherent right, inherent contradiction.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出法律与逻辑：固有权利、内在矛盾。

normal.en: Its nearest rival is intrinsic: inherent clings to a subject, intrinsic lies in its own nature.
normal.cn: 最接近的对手是 intrinsic：前者附着于主体，后者属于自身本质。

abstract.en: Picture moss growing inside a crack that no knife can reach.
abstract.cn: 想象青苔长在刀也够不到的裂缝里。

abstract.en: Picture a bell whose hum is part of its metal, not the air.
abstract.cn: 想象钟的余音来自金属本身，而不是空气。

abstract.en: Picture a rule that exists in the game itself, not on the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一条规则存在于游戏本身，而不是贴在墙上。

examples.en: There is an inherent danger in climbing without a rope.
examples.cn: 徒手攀爬存在固有危险。

examples.en: The design has an inherent flaw that no software patch can fix.
examples.cn: 这个设计存在任何补丁都修不好的内在缺陷。

examples.en: Patience is inherent in good teaching, not added later.
examples.cn: 耐心是好教学本身固有的，而不是后来添上的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印海里」——像印在海里一样去不掉，就是固有

root: 拉丁 haerere「粘住」→ inhaerere「粘在里面」→ 分词 inhaerens → 英语 inherent；同根词 adhere、hesitate、coherent。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe a quality stuck inside its owner: in matter, in a person, in a meaning, in a practice, in an office, in logic or in a body's defences.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述「粘在所有者内部」的性质：在材料里、在人身上、在词义里、在实践里、在职位里、在逻辑里，或在身体的防御里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a quality lodged inside a substance, impossible to peel off without destroying it.
core.cn: 核心意象：卡在物质内部的一种性质，剥下来就会毁掉该物。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL SIDE: what belongs to a substance or alloy rather than to its treatment.
branches.cn: 材料一面：属于物质或合金本身，而非加工带来的。

branches.en: THE PERSONAL SIDE: a trait present from birth.
branches.cn: 个人一面：出生时即有的特质。

branches.en: THE LINGUISTIC SIDE: a suggestion carried inside a word's meaning.
branches.cn: 语言一面：藏在词义里的暗示。

branches.en: THE BUILT-IN BURDEN: a risk tied to the practice, and a contradiction following from the definition.
branches.cn: 自带负担：与实践绑在一起的风险，以及由定义推出的矛盾。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTIONAL SIDE: powers held by an office, and defences present from the start.
branches.cn: 建制一面：职位自带的权利，以及从一开始就有的防御。

intro.en: Inherent is Latin in- 'in' plus haerere 'to stick', with the present participle ending -ens and the English adjective ending -ent.
intro.cn: inherent 由拉丁 in-「在内」与 haerere「粘住」构成，带现在分词词尾 -ens 与英语形容词词尾 -ent。

latinIntro.en: Haerere 'to stick' gives inhaerere 'to stick in'; its participle inhaerens gives the adjective, and the same root gives adhere and hesitate.
latinIntro.cn: haerere「粘住」给出 inhaerere「粘在里面」；其分词 inhaerens 给出形容词，同一词根还给出 adhere 与 hesitate。

items.example: The verb supplies the clinging image.

items.example: The ending gives inherence, the state of sticking in.

items.example: English added legal and scientific uses.
items.exampleCN: 英语加上了法律与科学用法。

items.example: The verb states the relation plainly.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词平实地陈述这种关系。

items.example: The adverb marks judgement by nature.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词标出「就本性而言」的判断。

items.example: The prefix reverses the direction of clinging.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀改变了「粘」的方向。

definition_en: concentrated on a small area or short period with great effort or input, rather than spread widely

scene: 训练营里，学员从早到晚反复练同一套动作，中间只留十分钟休息。The intensive training left the recruits exhausted by the third day.
sceneCN: 这里指在短时间内高强度地反复进行（第 1 个义项：投入大、密度高）；句意为这种强化训练到第三天就把新兵累垮了。

pos.zh: 高强度的；集中的；集约的

senses.title: Done with great effort in a short time
senses.definition: carried out with a high level of effort or activity packed into a short period
senses.definitionCN: 在很短的时间内塞进高强度的努力或活动
senses.example: They ran an intensive course over the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在夏天办了一期强化课程。
senses.why: The Latin participle meant stretched tight, so effort concentrated into little time is pictured as a taut string.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁分词意为「拉得很紧」，因此压进短时间的努力被想象成一根绷紧的弦。

senses.title: High input on a small area
senses.definition: using much labour, capital or chemical input on a limited area of land
senses.definitionCN: 在有限的土地上投入大量劳动、资本或化肥
senses.example: Intensive farming raises yields but can exhaust the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 集约耕作能提高产量，却可能耗尽地力。
senses.why: Agriculture contrasts putting much into little land with spreading a little over much land.
senses.whyCN: 农学把「往小片地里投很多」与「把一点投入摊到很多地」相对照。

senses.title: Concentrated and thorough
senses.definition: pursued closely and continuously until few gaps remain, said of study, search or treatment
senses.definitionCN: 紧密而持续地推进，直到几乎没有遗漏，用于学习、搜查或治疗
senses.example: The police began an intensive search of the building.
senses.exampleCN: 警方开始对这座建筑进行地毯式搜查。
senses.why: Attention that stays on one target without spreading out is the mental form of high concentration.
senses.whyCN: 注意力持续压在一个目标上而不分散，就是「高浓度」在脑力上的形态。

senses.title: Demanding much of one resource
senses.definition: used in compounds to say that a process uses a great deal of a particular resource
senses.definitionCN: 用于复合词，表示某过程消耗大量某类资源
senses.example: The industry is energy-intensive and sensitive to fuel prices.
senses.exampleCN: 这个行业属能源密集型，对燃料价格敏感。
senses.why: Whatever a process consumes heavily can be named before the adjective, as in labour-intensive or capital-intensive.
senses.whyCN: 某过程消耗得厉害的资源都可以放在这个词前面，如劳动密集型、资本密集型。

senses.title: A word used to stress another
senses.definition: in grammar, said of a form that adds emphasis rather than new meaning
senses.definitionCN: 语法中用于加强语气而不增添新意义的形式
senses.example: In 'I myself saw it', myself is an intensive pronoun.
senses.exampleCN: 在「我亲眼看见的」里，「我本人」就是强调代词。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the word for tension: an intensive form tightens a statement already made.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用了「拉紧」这个词：强调形式只是把已经说出的陈述再绷紧一次。

senses.title: Care for the most seriously ill
senses.definition: the ward or unit where patients needing constant monitoring are treated
senses.definitionCN: 持续监护最危重病人的病房或单元
senses.example: She spent two nights in intensive care after the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 事故后她在重症监护室住了两晚。
senses.why: The care is concentrated on a few patients with maximum attention, the medical version of density of effort.
senses.whyCN: 照护集中投给少数病人且注意力拉满，这是「投入密度」在医学里的形态。

senses.title: Reading for full understanding
senses.definition: reading a short text closely for every detail, as opposed to reading widely for gist
senses.definitionCN: 对短文本逐处细读以求细节，与为抓大意而泛读相对
senses.example: The class pairs intensive reading with extensive reading.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课把精读与泛读配在一起。
senses.why: Language teaching measures depth against breadth, and the deep side takes the word for concentration.
senses.whyCN: 语言教学用深度与广度对照，深的那一侧就用表示「集中」的词。

senses.title: Meaning defined by internal content
senses.titleCN: 由内部内容界定的意义
senses.definition: in logic, the set of properties that define a term, as opposed to the objects it covers
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑学中界定一个词项的性质集合，与它覆盖的对象相对
senses.example: The intensive definition lists the properties; the extensive one lists the members.
senses.exampleCN: 内涵定义列出性质，外延定义列出成员。
senses.why: Logic pairs the two: one looks inside for defining content, the other outward for range.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑把两者配对：一个向内看定义内容，一个向外看覆盖范围。

intro.en: Intensive comes from Latin intensus, the participle of intendere 'to stretch toward', from in- 'toward' and tendere 'to stretch'. English adopted it in the eighteenth century, and it became the partner of extensive in farming, logic and language teaching.
intro.cn: intensive 来自拉丁 intensus，即 intendere「朝……拉紧」的分词，由 in-「朝向」与 tendere「拉」构成。英语十八世纪采用它，并在农业、逻辑与语言教学中成为 extensive 的搭档。

items.en: Tendere meant to stretch or draw tight, and it also gives tension, tendon and extensive.
items.cn: tendere 意为伸或拉紧，也给出 tension、tendon 与 extensive。

items.en: With in- 'toward', intendere meant to stretch toward something, and later to aim attention at it.
items.cn: 加 in-「朝向」，intendere 意为朝某物拉紧，后来指把注意力对准它。

items.en: The participle intensus described a thing stretched tight, hence high in tension or force.
items.cn: 分词 intensus 形容被拉紧的东西，因而指张力或强度很高。

items.en: English intensive first described force and degree, then concentrated effort and concentrated farming.
items.cn: 英语的这个词先描述力度与程度，后指集中的努力与集中的耕作。

items.en: Agronomy and later economics set intensive against extensive: input per hectare against land area.
items.cn: 农学以及后来的经济学把「集约」与「粗放」相对：单位面积投入对土地面积。

items.en: Grammar uses intensive for emphasis, and logic for definition by internal properties, both keeping the idea of tension inside a small space.
items.cn: 语法用它表示强调，逻辑用它表示按内部性质下的定义，两者都保留「小空间内绷紧」之意。

note.en: The first group shares the tension stem; the second group includes its direct opposite and three words for concentrated effort.
note.cn: 第一组共享「拉紧」词干；第二组包含它的直接对立词，以及三个表示集中用力的词。

entries.definition: Very strong in feeling or degree; it describes the strength itself, not how work is organised.
entries.definitionCN: 感情或程度非常强烈；描述强度本身，而非工作的组织方式。

entries.definition: The measurable strength of something; the noun of degree rather than of method.
entries.definitionCN: 某物可量度的强度；是程度名词，不是方法名词。

entries.definition: To make stronger or more concentrated; it names the increase.
entries.definitionCN: 使更强或更集中；命名「加强」这一变化。

entries.definition: In a concentrated way; it modifies how an activity is carried out.
entries.definitionCN: 以集中的方式；修饰活动的进行方式。

entries.definition: Spread over a wide area with low input per unit; the exact opposite strategy in farming, study and physics.
entries.definitionCN: 大面积铺开、单位投入低；在农业、学习与物理中都是完全相反的策略。

entries.definition: Brought together into one place or focus; it stresses gathering rather than high input.
entries.definitionCN: 汇集到一处或一个焦点；强调集中到一处，而非高投入。

entries.definition: Strict and thorough in method; it judges standards of accuracy, not density of effort.
entries.definitionCN: 方法上严格彻底；评价的是精确标准，而非投入密度。

entries.definition: Leaving nothing out; it stresses completeness, while the target word stresses concentration.
entries.definitionCN: 什么都不遗漏；强调完整，而目标词强调集中。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'stretch tight': intensive work is a string pulled hard over a small space.
normal.cn: 词根意为「拉紧」：高强度的工作就是一小段被拉得很紧的弦。

normal.en: The family runs intense, intensity, intensify and intensively.
normal.cn: 同族词包括强烈的、强度、加强、集中地。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark effort: intensive training, intensive research, intensive reading.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用力：强化训练、集中研究、精读。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark land and medicine: intensive farming, intensive care.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出土地与医疗：集约农业、重症监护。

normal.en: Its built-in partner is extensive: one counts input per area, the other counts area covered.
normal.cn: 它的固定搭档是 extensive：一个数单位面积投入，一个数覆盖面积。

abstract.en: Picture a whole year of lessons squeezed into six weeks.
abstract.cn: 想象一整年的课程被压进六周。

abstract.en: Picture one hectare watered by ten people instead of one.
abstract.cn: 想象一公顷地由十个人而不是一个人来浇。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp whose beam is narrowed until it burns a hole.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯把光收窄到能烧出一个洞。

examples.en: The hospital opened a new intensive care unit last month.
examples.cn: 医院上个月启用了新的重症监护病房。

examples.en: Intensive agriculture feeds more people per hectare.
examples.cn: 集约农业每公顷能养活更多人。

examples.en: Two weeks of intensive study prepared her for the exam.
examples.cn: 两周的密集学习让她做好了考试准备。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all concentrate something into a small space or a short time: effort, capital, attention, grammatical force, medical care, reading depth or defining content.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把某样东西压进小空间或短时间：努力、资本、注意力、语法力度、医疗照护、阅读深度或定义内容。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a string pulled tight, so all the force sits inside a short length.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根被拉紧的弦，全部力量都集中在很短的一段里。

branches.en: THE TIME SIDE: heavy effort packed into a short course or drill.
branches.cn: 时间一面：把高强度努力塞进短课程或短训练。

branches.en: THE INPUT SIDE: much labour or capital on little land, and compounds naming the resource consumed.
branches.cn: 投入一面：小片地上大量劳动或资本，以及命名所耗资源的复合词。

branches.en: THE NARROWED SIDE: close continuous search, and constant monitoring of the sickest patients.
branches.cn: 收窄一面：持续细密的搜查，以及对最危重病人的持续监护。

branches.en: THE DEPTH SIDE: grammatical emphasis, and reading a short text for every detail.
branches.cn: 深度一面：语法强调，以及把短文读到每一处细节。

branches.en: THE LOGICAL SIDE: definition by internal properties, paired against extent of range.
branches.cn: 逻辑一面：按内部性质下的定义，与外延范围相对。
