由该形容词加表示方式的副词后缀构成，义为「居中地」
由「居间调解」的动词加表示动作结果的名词后缀构成，义为「居间调解；中介作用」
由同一「居中」词根加表示施动者的后缀构成，义为「中间人；居间的」
由该形容词与表示「宿主」的名词构成的固定复合词，义为「中间宿主」

senses.title: A level between beginner and advanced
senses.titleCN: 难度介于初级与高级之间
senses.definition: situated at the middle level of a course, skill or examination
senses.definitionCN: 处于课程、技能或考试的中间层级
senses.example: The school offers beginner, intermediate and advanced groups.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校开设初级、中级与高级班。
senses.why: The Latin word literally means 'that which is between', so a middle rung of learning is its plainest use.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词字面就是「处于两者之间者」，因此学习阶梯的中间一级是它最平实的用法。

senses.title: Placed between two points
senses.definition: located in the middle of a space or between two other positions
senses.definitionCN: 位于某个空间的中央，或处于另外两个位置之间
senses.example: An intermediate station lies halfway along the line.
senses.exampleCN: 线路上正好中段设有一个中间站。
senses.why: Space is the original ground of the word: one position with others on either side.
senses.whyCN: 空间是这个词最原本的地面：一个位置，两侧各另有位置。

senses.title: A stage between start and end
senses.definition: marking a transitional step in a process that has a beginning and an end
senses.definitionCN: 标出一个有始有终的流程中的过渡步骤
senses.example: The project is at an intermediate stage of review.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目处在评审的中间阶段。
senses.why: Time and process can be laid out as a line, and the middle section is intermediate.
senses.whyCN: 时间与流程可以摊成一条线，中间那一段就是「居间」的。

senses.title: A substance formed on the way
senses.definition: a chemical species produced in one step of a reaction and consumed in another
senses.definitionCN: 在反应某一步生成、又在另一步被消耗的化学物种
senses.example: The reaction passes through a short-lived intermediate.
senses.exampleCN: 这个反应会经过一种寿命很短的中间产物。
senses.why: Chemistry maps reactions as paths, and whatever sits on the path between reactants and products is intermediate.
senses.whyCN: 化学把反应画成路径，位于反应物与产物之间路径上的东西就是中间产物。

senses.title: A person who stands between sides
senses.definition: someone who carries messages or settles matters between two parties
senses.definitionCN: 在双方之间传话或调停事务的人
senses.example: The bank acted as an intermediate in the sale.
senses.exampleCN: 银行在交易中充当了中间人。
senses.why: A go-between occupies the middle position socially, so the adjective turns into a person noun.
senses.whyCN: 中间人在社交上占据「中间位置」，于是形容词转为指人的名词。

senses.title: A relay point in a route or network
senses.titleCN: 线路或网络中的中继点
senses.definition: a node or stop that passes something onward between an origin and a destination
senses.definitionCN: 在起点与终点之间把东西转送出去的节点或站点
senses.example: Packets cross several intermediate nodes before arrival.
senses.exampleCN: 数据包在到达前会经过若干中继节点。
senses.why: A route with more than one leg has a middle leg, and its endpoints are intermediate.
senses.whyCN: 由多段组成的路线有一段在中，它的端点就是「居间」的。

senses.title: A period between two dates
senses.definition: said of a period that falls between two named events or dates
senses.definitionCN: 用于落在两个明确事件或日期之间的时段
senses.example: An intermediate period of calm followed the first storm.
senses.exampleCN: 第一场风暴之后有一段短暂的平静期。
senses.why: Calendar time also has intervals, and the interval between two dates takes the middle word.
senses.whyCN: 日历时间也有间隔，两个日期之间的那一段就用了「中间」这个词。

senses.title: An organism hosting a parasite's middle stage
senses.titleCN: 寄生物中间阶段所寄居的生物
senses.definition: in parasitology, the host in which a parasite develops through its larval stage
senses.definitionCN: 寄生物学中寄生物度过幼虫阶段所寄居的宿主
senses.example: Snails serve as the intermediate host for the liver fluke.
senses.exampleCN: 螺类是肝吸虫的中间宿主。
senses.why: The parasite has two hosts in sequence, and the one in the middle is named by this adjective.
senses.whyCN: 寄生物按顺序有两个宿主，位于中间的那个就用这个形容词命名。

intro.en: Intermediate is Latin intermedius 'that which is between', from inter 'between' and medius 'middle'. English took it in the sixteenth century; chemistry and parasitology added their own middle stages later. The formation is clear; first dates are approximate.
intro.cn: intermediate 是拉丁 intermedius「处于两者之间者」，由 inter「之间」与 medius「中间」构成。英语十六世纪引入；化学与寄生物学后来各自加上自己的「中间阶段」。构词清楚，首见年代为约数。

items.en: Inter meant between or among, and it is the prefix behind intercity, international and intervene.
items.cn: inter 意为在……之间或之中，是 intercity、international、intervene 等词的前缀。

items.en: Medius meant middle, and it also gives medium, median and immediate.
items.cn: medius 意为中间，也给出 medium、median 与 immediate。

items.en: The compound adjective meant lying between two things, and it applied to space, time and rank.
items.cn: 这个复合形容词意为处在两物之间，用于空间、时间与等级。

items.en: English intermediate first described middle positions and middle ranks, then middle stages of processes.
items.cn: 英语的这个词先描述中间位置与中间等级，后指流程的中间阶段。

items.en: Nineteenth-century chemistry named short-lived species on a reaction path intermediates.
items.cn: 十九世纪化学把反应路径上寿命很短的物种称为中间产物。

items.en: Parasitology distinguishes the intermediate host from the final host in a parasite's life cycle.
items.cn: 寄生物学在寄生物生活史中区别中间宿主与终宿主。

note.en: The first group shares the middle root; the second group holds words for middle position and transition.
note.cn: 第一组共享「中间」词根；第二组是表示中间位置与过渡的词。

entries.definition: A person or body that carries messages between sides; a person noun, not a level.
entries.definitionCN: 在双方之间传递消息的人或机构；是人或机构名词，不是层级。

entries.definition: The work of standing between parties, especially in finance; it names the function.
entries.definitionCN: 在双方之间居间的工作，尤用于金融；命名的是职能。

entries.definition: The state of being in the middle; a formal abstract noun.
entries.definitionCN: 处于中间的状态；正式的抽象名词。

entries.definition: In a middle position or degree; it is rare outside technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 处于中间位置或程度；技术文字之外少见。

entries.definition: The general word for the central part; it does not imply a scale with named levels.
entries.definitionCN: 表示中央部分的通用词；不暗示有具名层级的尺度。

entries.definition: The middle value in a ranked set; a statistical term, not a position between two objects.
entries.definitionCN: 排序数据集中的中间值；是统计术语，不是两物之间的位置。

entries.definition: Belonging to a change from one state to another; it stresses the change rather than the position.
entries.definitionCN: 属于从一种状态到另一种状态的转变；强调变化而非位置。

entries.definition: Not extreme in amount or degree; it judges intensity, not rank on a ladder.
entries.definitionCN: 数量或程度不极端；评价强度，而非阶梯上的等级。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Inter means 'between' and medius means 'middle': the word says both at once.
normal.cn: inter 意为「之间」，medius 意为「中间」：这个词把两层意思叠在一起。

normal.en: The family runs intermediary, intermediation, intermediacy and intermediately.
normal.cn: 同族词包括中间人、居间调解、居中状态、居中地。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark levels and stages: intermediate level, intermediate stage.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出层级与阶段：中级水平、中间阶段。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark science: intermediate host, intermediate product.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出科学用法：中间宿主、中间产物。

normal.en: It sits between immediate and distant, between beginner and advanced.
normal.cn: 它夹在「直接」与「遥远」之间，也夹在初级与高级之间。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase with one step exactly halfway, painted neither colour.
abstract.cn: 想象楼梯正中间那一级，两种颜色都没刷。

abstract.en: Picture a relay runner who only hands the baton onward.
abstract.cn: 想象接力跑者只负责把棒交出去。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge stone carrying weight from one bank to the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一块桥石把重量从一岸传到另一岸。

examples.en: The textbook is written for intermediate learners.
examples.cn: 这本教材是为中级学习者写的。

examples.en: There is an intermediate stage between planning and building.
examples.cn: 规划与建造之间还有一个中间阶段。

examples.en: A broker serves as an intermediate between buyer and seller.
examples.cn: 经纪人在买卖双方之间充当中间人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特米第」——在中间的那一「第」，就是中间层级

root: 拉丁 inter「之间」+ medius「中间」→ intermedius「处于之间者」→ 英语 intermediate；同族 intermediary、intermediation、immediate。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one position: between. It may be between levels, points in space, stages, chemicals, people, network nodes, dates or hosts.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一个位置：在两者之间。可以是层级之间、空间两点之间、阶段之间、化学物质之间、人与人之间、网络节点之间、日期之间，或宿主之间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one station on a line with a station on each side of it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条线上的一个站，左右各还有一个站。

branches.en: THE SCALE SIDE: a middle level of learning, and a period between two dates.
branches.cn: 尺度一面：学习的中间层级，以及两日期之间的时段。

branches.en: THE SPATIAL SIDE: a position halfway, and a relay node on a route.
branches.cn: 空间一面：半途的位置，以及路线上的中继节点。

branches.en: THE PROCESS SIDE: a transitional step between beginning and end.
branches.cn: 流程一面：起止之间的过渡步骤。

branches.en: THE CHEMICAL SIDE: a species formed on the way from reactants to products.
branches.cn: 化学一面：从反应物到产物途中生成的物种。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL AND BIOLOGICAL SIDE: a go-between person, and a host holding a parasite's larval stage.
branches.cn: 社会与生物一面：居间的中间人，以及承载寄生物幼虫阶段的宿主。

intro.en: Intermediate is Latin inter 'between' plus medius 'middle' plus an adjective ending; English adds endings for state, manner and agency.
intro.cn: intermediate 由拉丁 inter「之间」、medius「中间」与形容词词尾组成；英语再加表示状态、方式与施动的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Inter 'between' plus medius 'middle' gives intermedius, the direct source of the English adjective.
latinIntro.cn: inter「之间」加 medius「中间」得出 intermedius，即英语形容词的直接来源。

items.example: The prefix sets the middle position.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀定出「中间」的位置。

items.example: The adjective supplies the centre.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供「中央」之意。

items.example: The compound applies to space, time and rank.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词用于空间、时间与等级。

items.example: The ending makes the compound an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把复合词变成形容词。

items.example: English extended it to chemistry and biology.
items.exampleCN: 英语把它扩展到化学与生物学。

items.example: The suffix gives the abstract state noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀给出抽象状态名词。

items.example: The suffix gives the rare manner adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀给出少见的方式副词。

items.example: The suffix builds the name of the mediating function.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀造出「居间职能」的名称。

items.example: The ending builds intermediary, the person noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾造出指人的「中间人」。

items.example: The same adjective also gives medium and median.
items.exampleCN: 同一个形容词也给出 medium 与 median。

derivatives.zh: 由词干加状态名词后缀构成，义为「居中状态」
由该形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「居中地」
由「居间」加动作名词后缀构成，义为「中介作用」
由同一词根加施动后缀构成，义为「中间人」

definition_zh: 内在本质的；本身价值的；内在动机的；内禀的；内部的（肌肉）；内蕴的（曲率）；本征的（半导体）；内生的（增长）
definition_en: belonging to the inner nature of a thing and measured without reference to anything outside it
core_image: 拍卖台上摆着一幅无人出价的旧素描，鉴定师却只说它的价值不在标签上
scene: 拍卖行把一幅无人问津的旧素描摆上台面，鉴定师却说它的分量不在价签上。The old sketch has an intrinsic worth that no auction price can measure.
sceneCN: 这里指事物自身所具有、不由外界定价的价值（第 2 个义项：不依赖外部评价的内在价值）；句意为这幅旧素描有一种拍卖价量不出的内在价值。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示方式的副词后缀构成，义为「本质上；就其自身而言」
由该形容词的词干加表示性质的名词后缀构成，义为「内在性；固有性」，多用于哲学
由对应的拉丁「在外」形式进入英语，义为「外在的；外来的」，是与目标词成对的反义对照词

senses.title: Belonging to a thing's own nature
senses.definition: forming part of what something is in itself, independent of how others regard it
senses.definitionCN: 构成某物自身之所是，与别人如何看待它无关
senses.example: Curiosity seems intrinsic to the human mind.
senses.exampleCN: 好奇心似乎是人心本身固有的。
senses.why: The Latin word meant 'on the inside', so a quality located within a thing's own nature is intrinsic.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词意为「在内侧」，因此位于事物自身本性之中的性质就是内在的。

senses.title: Worth that is not set by a market
senses.definition: value that a thing has in itself, apart from price, usefulness or what buyers will pay
senses.definitionCN: 事物自身即有的价值，与价格、用途或买家的出价无关
senses.example: Philosophers debate whether art has intrinsic value.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家争论艺术是否具有内在价值。
senses.why: If worth is inside the thing, then an outside price can measure it only indirectly, if at all.
senses.whyCN: 如果价值在事物内部，那么外部价格至多只能间接地量到它。

senses.title: Drive that comes from within
senses.definition: motivation arising from interest or enjoyment rather than from external reward or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 由兴趣或乐趣产生的动机，而非来自外部奖励或压力
senses.example: Intrinsic motivation keeps volunteers coming back.
senses.exampleCN: 内在动机让志愿者一再回来。
senses.why: The source of the drive sits inside the person, which is exactly what the word locates inside.
senses.whyCN: 动力的源头在人的内部，而这正是这个词所定位的「内侧」。

senses.title: A property independent of amount
senses.titleCN: 与数量多少无关的性质
senses.definition: in physics, a property of a material that does not change when the sample size changes
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中不随样品大小改变的材料性质
senses.example: Density is intrinsic; mass is not.
senses.exampleCN: 密度是内禀性质，质量不是。
senses.why: A property that stays the same whether you take a gram or a tonne belongs to the substance itself.
senses.whyCN: 无论取一克还是一吨都不变的性质，属于物质自身。

senses.title: Muscles lying inside an organ
senses.definition: in anatomy, said of muscles whose origin and insertion lie within the structure they move
senses.definitionCN: 解剖学中起止点都位于其所运动结构内部的肌肉
senses.example: The intrinsic muscles of the hand control the fingers finely.
senses.exampleCN: 手部内在肌精细地控制手指。
senses.why: Anatomy contrasts muscles inside an organ with ones that enter it from outside.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学把器官内部的肌肉与从外部伸入的肌肉相对照。

senses.title: Curvature measurable from inside
senses.definition: in geometry, a curvature determined by measurements within the surface itself, without embedding it in a larger space
senses.definitionCN: 几何中只靠曲面内部的测量即可确定的曲率，无需把曲面嵌入更大空间
senses.example: Intrinsic curvature can be detected by triangles on the surface.
senses.exampleCN: 内蕴曲率可以通过曲面上的三角形测出。
senses.why: If the measurement needs nothing outside, the property is literally intrinsic to the surface.
senses.whyCN: 若测量不需要任何外部条件，该性质就字面地内在于曲面之中。

senses.title: Pure, undoped material
senses.definition: in electronics, said of a semiconductor whose behaviour comes from its own pure crystal, with no added impurities
senses.definitionCN: 电子学中行为来自纯净晶体本身、未添加杂质的半导体
senses.example: Intrinsic silicon conducts far less than doped silicon.
senses.exampleCN: 本征硅的导电性远低于掺杂硅。
senses.why: Its electrical behaviour is a property of the pure material, not of anything added from outside.
senses.whyCN: 它的电学行为来自纯净材料本身，而不是外部添加物。

senses.title: Growth generated from inside
senses.definition: in economics, growth produced by internal factors such as knowledge and investment in people, not by outside shocks
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中由知识、对人的投资等内部因素产生的增长，而非外部冲击带来
senses.example: Intrinsic growth models stress education over foreign aid.
senses.exampleCN: 内生增长模型强调教育胜过外国援助。
senses.why: The model looks for the causes of growth inside the economy rather than outside it.
senses.whyCN: 这类模型在经济体内部寻找增长原因，而不是在外部寻找。

intro.en: Intrinsic comes from Late Latin intrinsecus 'inwardly, on the inside', built on intra 'within' and secus 'alongside'. French intrinsèque carried it into English in the seventeenth century, paired with extrinsic. The direct source is clear; the earlier makeup of secus is still debated.
intro.cn: intrinsic 来自晚期拉丁 intrinsecus「向内的、在内侧的」，由 intra「在内」与 secus「沿着、旁边」构成。法语 intrinsèque 在十七世纪把它带进英语，并与 extrinsic 成对。直接来源清楚；更早的 secus 构成仍有争议。

items.en: Intra meant within or inside, and it still appears in English words such as intravenous.
items.cn: intra 意为在……之内，至今出现在 intravenous 等英语词中。

items.en: Secus meant alongside or beside; its further origin is disputed, so the internal makeup of the compound is not certain.
items.cn: secus 意为沿着、在旁边；它更早的来源有争议，因此这个复合词的内部构成并非确证。

items.en: The adverb meant inward or on the inside, and it described what belongs to a thing from within.
items.cn: 这个副词意为向内、在内侧，描述从内部属于某物的东西。

items.en: Its partner meant from outside, and the pair intrinsic and extrinsic still divide inner nature from external circumstance.
items.cn: 与之配对的形式意为「从外部」，如今「内在」与「外在」这一对仍用于区分本性与外部环境。

items.en: English took intrinsic through French for qualities belonging to a thing itself, especially in philosophy and theology.
items.cn: 英语经法语引入这个词，用于属于事物自身的性质，尤其在哲学与神学中。

items.en: Physics, anatomy, geometry and economics each gave the word a measured meaning where 'inside' can be tested.
items.cn: 物理学、解剖学、几何学与经济学各自给这个词一个可检验的「内部」含义。

note.en: The first group is the same word family with its opposite; the second group holds near synonyms that locate qualities differently.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词族及其对立词；第二组是同样描述性质归属、但定位方式不同的近义词。

entries.definition: By its own nature, without reference to outside standards; it marks the source of value.
entries.definitionCN: 就其自身本性而言，不参照外部标准；标出价值的来源。

entries.definition: The quality of belonging to a thing's inner nature; a rare philosophical noun.
entries.definitionCN: 属于事物内在本性的性质；少见的哲学名词。

entries.definition: Coming from outside, such as reward, price or circumstance; the exact opposite partner.
entries.definitionCN: 来自外部的东西，如奖励、价格或环境；正是与之相对的另一半。

entries.definition: An older variant spelling of the same adjective, now mostly replaced by the shorter form.
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词的较早异体拼法，如今多被较短的形取代。

entries.definition: Stuck to a subject so that it cannot be removed; it stresses attachment, while the target word stresses inner nature.
entries.definitionCN: 附着于主体而无法去除；强调「附着」，而目标词强调「内在本质」。

entries.definition: Present from birth; it marks a starting point in time rather than a location inside a nature.
entries.definitionCN: 出生时即有；标出时间上的起点，而非本性内部的位置。

entries.definition: Belonging to the essence, so that without it the thing would not be itself; stronger than a mere inner quality.
entries.definitionCN: 属于本质，缺了它事物就不成其为自身；比单纯「内在性质」更强。

entries.definition: Designed into a product; the everyday word for what is installed rather than grown from within.
entries.definitionCN: 设计进产品里的；是日常说法，指装进去而非从内部长出来的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means 'within': intrinsic value is the value inside the thing, not on the price tag.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「在内」：内在价值是事物里面的价值，不在价签上。

normal.en: The family runs intrinsically, intrinsicality and the paired opposite extrinsic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括本质上、内在性，以及与它成对的外在的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark value and drive: intrinsic value, intrinsic motivation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出价值与动力：内在价值、内在动机。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark science: intrinsic property, intrinsic semiconductor.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出科学用法：内禀性质、本征半导体。

normal.en: Its opposite is extrinsic, which puts the source outside the thing.
normal.cn: 它的对立词是 extrinsic，把来源放在事物外部。

abstract.en: Picture a coin whose shine comes from its own metal, not the light in the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币的光泽来自它自己的金属，而不是房间里的灯。

abstract.en: Picture a runner who trains because the running itself feels good.
abstract.cn: 想象一个跑者训练，因为跑这件事本身让他舒服。

abstract.en: Picture a room whose warmth comes from its stones, not from a heater.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子的暖意来自石头本身，而不是暖气。

examples.en: The painting's intrinsic value lies in its brushwork, not its price.
examples.cn: 这幅画的内在价值在笔法，而不在价格。

examples.en: Children learn faster when motivation is intrinsic.
examples.cn: 当动机来自内心时，孩子学得更快。

examples.en: Conductivity is an intrinsic property of the pure crystal.
examples.cn: 导电性是纯晶体的内禀性质。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印吹壳」——印在壳子最里面那一层，从外看不见，就是内在的

root: 拉丁 intra「在内」+ secus「沿着、旁边」→ 晚期拉丁 intrinsecus「内侧的」→ 法语 intrinsèque → 英语 intrinsic；与 extrinsecus「外在的」成对。secus 的更早来源尚有争议。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all place a quality inside its owner: in a nature, a value, a motive, a material property, an organ, a surface, a crystal or an economy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把某种性质放在所有者内部：放在本性里、价值里、动机里、材料性质里、器官里、曲面里、晶体里，或经济体里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a quality that lives inside a thing, so outside measures can only approach it.
core.cn: 核心意象：住在事物内部的一种性质，外部量度只能靠近它。

branches.en: THE NATURE SENSE: what a thing is in itself, apart from outside opinion.
branches.cn: 本性义：某物自身之所是，与外部看法无关。

branches.en: THE VALUED AND MOTIVATED SIDE: worth not set by a market, and interest that needs no reward.
branches.cn: 价值与动力一面：不由市场定价的价值，以及无需奖励的兴趣。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL SIDE: properties unchanged by sample size, and the behaviour of a pure crystal.
branches.cn: 材料一面：不随样品大小改变的性质，以及纯晶体自身的行为。

branches.en: THE ANATOMICAL SIDE: muscles whose ends both lie inside the organ they move.
branches.cn: 解剖一面：两端都在所运动器官内部的肌肉。

branches.en: THE SELF-CONTAINED SIDE: curvature measured within a surface, and growth generated inside an economy.
branches.cn: 自足一面：在曲面内部测得的曲率，以及经济体内部产生的增长。

intro.en: Intrinsic is a Latin adverb turned adjective: intra 'within' plus secus 'alongside', with the adjective ending -ic.
intro.cn: intrinsic 是由拉丁副词转成的形容词：intra「在内」加 secus「沿着」，再加形容词词尾 -ic。

latinIntro.en: Intra plus secus gives the adverb intrinsecus 'inwardly'; the adjective form, through French, is intrinsèque, taken into English as intrinsic.
latinIntro.cn: intra 加 secus 得出副词 intrinsecus「向内」；其形容词形式经法语作 intrinsèque，进入英语成为 intrinsic。

items.example: The prefix locates the quality inside.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把性质定位在内部。

items.example: Its earlier origin is disputed, so the compound is not fully certain.
items.exampleCN: 它更早的来源有争议，因此该复合词并非完全确证。

items.example: The adverb is the direct source of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词是形容词的直接来源。

items.example: The counterpart gives the paired opposite in English.
items.exampleCN: 配对形式给出英语中的反义对照词。

items.example: The ending makes an adjective of the adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把副词变成形容词。

items.example: English added measurable technical senses.
items.exampleCN: 英语加上了可量度的技术义。

items.example: The ending gives the manner adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾给出方式副词。

items.example: The suffix names the inner quality in philosophy.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀在哲学中命名「内在性」。

items.example: The longer form is now archaic.
items.exampleCN: 较长的形式如今已属古旧。

items.example: The opposite partner appears in the same technical fields.
items.exampleCN: 这个对立词出现在同一批技术领域。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「本质上」
由该形容词词干加性质名词后缀构成，义为「内在性」
由对应的「在外」形式进入英语，义为「外在的」

definition_zh: 被隔离的；偏僻的；零星的；孤立无援的；医学隔离的；电气上隔离的；孤立系统的；分离提纯的
definition_en: separated from other people, places or things, so that little or no contact remains
core_image: 山间小屋在大雪之后与公路断了联系，补给只能靠直升机空投
scene: 大雪过后，山间那间小屋与公路断了联系，补给只能靠直升机空投。The farm was isolated by the flood for five days.
sceneCN: 这里指与外界断绝往来、接不上联系（第 1 个义项：被隔开、失去接触）；句意为洪水让这座农场与外界隔绝了五天。

derivatives.zh: 由「使隔离」的动词加表示动作结果的名词后缀构成，义为「隔离；孤立状态」
由拉丁「岛」的形容词形式经法语与意大利语进入英语，义为「使隔离；分离出」
由「使隔离」的动词加表示器械或施动者的名词后缀构成，义为「隔离器；隔离装置」
由「使隔离」的动词加表示「可……的」的形容词后缀构成，义为「可隔离的；可分离的」
由同一动词加更完整的「可……的」后缀构成，义为「可分离出来的」，常用于实验语境

senses.title: Cut off from contact
senses.definition: separated from others so that communication, supply or movement is blocked
senses.definitionCN: 与他人隔开，使通讯、补给或往来中断
senses.example: The village was isolated by the landslide for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 山体滑坡让这个村子与外界隔绝了一周。
senses.why: The root is the Latin word for an island: land entirely surrounded by water is the original picture of being cut off.
senses.whyCN: 词根是拉丁语的「岛」：四面环水的陆地，正是「被隔断」最初的那幅画。

senses.title: Far from other settlements
senses.definition: situated at a distance from towns and services, so that few people come near
senses.definitionCN: 离城镇与服务设施很远，因而很少有人靠近
senses.example: They bought an isolated cottage above the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在山谷上方买下一间偏僻的小屋。
senses.why: Distance produces isolation, so a place with few neighbours is described by the same word.
senses.whyCN: 距离造成隔绝，因此邻居稀少的地方就用同一个词来形容。

senses.title: A single case standing apart
senses.definition: occurring singly and not as part of a pattern, so it is unlikely to repeat
senses.definitionCN: 单独发生，不属于某种模式的一部分，因而不太可能重演
senses.example: Officials called the outbreak an isolated case.
senses.exampleCN: 官员称这次疫情是一起孤立病例。
senses.why: One instance standing apart from a series is like one island standing apart from a coast.
senses.whyCN: 从一串事件中单独分出来的一个实例，就像脱离海岸的一座孤岛。

senses.title: Socially cut off from others
senses.definition: having little or no contact with family, friends or community, often unwillingly
senses.definitionCN: 与家人、朋友或社区几乎没有往来，常非出于自愿
senses.example: Many elderly residents feel isolated after moving here.
senses.exampleCN: 许多老年居民搬到这里后感到被孤立。
senses.why: A person can be an island too, with contact routes closed on every side.
senses.whyCN: 人也可以是一座岛，四周的联系通道全部关闭。

senses.title: Kept apart to stop spread
senses.definition: separated from healthy people or animals to prevent a disease from spreading
senses.definitionCN: 与健康的人或动物分开，以防疾病扩散
senses.example: Patients with the fever were isolated in a separate ward.
senses.exampleCN: 发热病人被隔离在单独的病房里。
senses.why: Medicine deliberately makes a case an island so that infection cannot cross the water.
senses.whyCN: 医学有意把病例变成一座岛，让传染无法渡水而过。

senses.title: Electrically separated
senses.definition: said of a circuit or device that has no conductive path to another circuit
senses.definitionCN: 用于与另一电路之间没有导电通路的电路或装置
senses.example: An isolated supply protects the instrument from surges.
senses.exampleCN: 隔离电源能保护仪器免受电涌冲击。
senses.why: No conductive path means no bridging, the technical form of an island with no causeway.
senses.whyCN: 没有导电路径就没有桥接，这是「没有堤道相连的岛」的技术形态。

senses.title: Sealed off in thermodynamics
senses.titleCN: 热力学中与外界完全封隔
senses.definition: said of a system that exchanges neither matter nor energy with its surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 用于与外界既不交换物质也不交换能量的系统
senses.example: An isolated system keeps its total energy constant.
senses.exampleCN: 孤立系统保持总能量不变。
senses.why: Physics pushes the island idea to its limit: nothing at all crosses the boundary.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把「岛」的想法推到极限：没有任何东西越过边界。

senses.title: Separated out in a laboratory
senses.titleCN: 在实验室中单独分离出来
senses.definition: obtained alone and free of other substances, as a compound, gene or strain
senses.definitionCN: 单独取得、不含其他物质，如化合物、基因或菌株
senses.example: The team isolated the protein from a few grams of tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 团队从几克组织里分离出了这种蛋白质。
senses.why: Taking one thing out of a mixture puts it on its own, which is isolation in the laboratory.
senses.whyCN: 把一样东西从混合物中取出、让它单独存在，就是实验室里的隔离。

intro.en: Isolated comes through French isolé and Italian isolato from Latin insulatus 'made into an island', from insula 'island'. English adopted it in the eighteenth century. The chain is well recorded; first dates are approximate.
intro.cn: isolated 经法语 isolé 与意大利语 isolato 上溯拉丁 insulatus「被造成岛屿的」，后者源于 insula「岛」。英语十八世纪采用。构词链记录清楚，首见年代为约数。

items.en: Insula meant island, and it also named a block of buildings in Rome, each block like a separate island.
items.cn: insula 意为岛，也指罗马城中一栋独立的街区，每栋都像一座单独的岛。

items.en: The adjective meant made into an island or cut off as if by water, and it is the direct source of the whole family.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为「被造成岛、像被水隔开」，是整个词族的直接来源。

items.en: Italian used isolato for a person or place standing alone, and the word spread with Italian art and trade.
items.cn: 意大利语用这个词指独自存在的人或地点，该词随意大利艺术与贸易传播。

items.en: French isolé carried the sense of being set apart, and English borrowed the participle as isolated.
items.cn: 法语 isolé 带有「被分开放置」之意，英语把这个分词借为 isolated。

items.en: English first used it of places and buildings, then of people, cases and specimens.
items.cn: 英语最初用它指地点与建筑，后来扩展到人、案例与标本。

items.en: Medicine, electrical engineering and thermodynamics each gave the word a precise boundary that nothing may cross.
items.cn: 医学、电气工程与热力学各自给这个词一条不得越过的精确边界。

note.en: The first group shares the island stem; the second group holds words for apartness that come from distance, feeling or deliberate separation.
note.cn: 第一组共享「岛」词干；第二组是表示「分开」的词，来源分别是距离、感受或有意分隔。

entries.definition: The state or act of being set apart; the noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 被隔开的状态或行为；是形容词背后的名词。

entries.definition: To set something apart, or to separate a substance from a mixture.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物隔开，或从混合物中分离出某物质。

entries.definition: A device that keeps one part from affecting another; a technical object noun.
entries.definitionCN: 使一部分不受另一部分影响的装置；是技术性的器物名词。

entries.definition: Able to be separated out; it states a possibility rather than a state.
entries.definitionCN: 能够被分离出来；说的是可能性而非状态。

entries.definition: Far away in distance; it measures how far, not whether contact exists.
entries.definitionCN: 距离上很远；量的是远近，而不是有没有联系。

entries.definition: Feeling sad because one lacks company; it reports a feeling, not an objective separation.
entries.definitionCN: 因缺少陪伴而难过；说的是感受，而非客观的隔断。

entries.definition: Deliberately hidden away and quiet; it often suggests a chosen retreat.
entries.definitionCN: 有意隐藏、清静；常暗示主动选择的退居之处。

entries.definition: Physically or socially disconnected; the everyday phrase for the result the target word names.
entries.definitionCN: 在物理或社交上断开；是目标词所指结果的日常说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root is Latin for island: to isolate is to make something an island.
normal.cn: 词根是拉丁语的「岛」：隔离就是把某物变成一座岛。

normal.en: The family runs isolate, isolation, isolator and isolable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括隔离、隔离状态、隔离器、可隔离的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the social side: isolated case, socially isolated.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出社会一面：个别案例、社会孤立。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark technical use: isolated system, isolated gene.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术用法：孤立系统、分离出的基因。

normal.en: Two neighbours differ: remote measures distance, lonely measures feeling.
normal.cn: 两个近邻不同：remote 量距离，lonely 量感受。

abstract.en: Picture a house on a rock with water on every side and no bridge.
abstract.cn: 想象一座房子立在礁石上，四周都是水，没有桥。

abstract.en: Picture one red apple in a crate of green ones.
abstract.cn: 想象一箱青苹果里只有一只红的。

abstract.en: Picture a phone with every contact deleted except one.
abstract.cn: 想象一部手机，联系人删到只剩一个。

examples.en: The islanders live isolated from the mainland for half the year.
examples.cn: 这些岛民一年里有半年与大陆隔绝。

examples.en: Doctors isolated the virus before it could spread.
examples.cn: 医生在病毒扩散前把它分离了出来。

examples.en: His office is isolated from the rest of the team.
examples.cn: 他的办公室与团队其他成员隔开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱搜累他」——一个人被隔在小岛上，找不到人也靠不上，就是孤立

root: 拉丁 insula「岛」→ insulatus「被造成岛的、像被水隔开的」→ 意大利语 isolato、法语 isolé → 英语 isolated。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all make something an island: a place, a person, a single case, a patient, a circuit, a physical system or a compound taken out of a mixture.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把某物变成一座岛：地方、人、单个案例、病人、电路、物理系统，或从混合物中取出的化合物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a piece of land surrounded by water, with no bridge to the mainland.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块四面环水的陆地，没有桥连到大陆。

branches.en: THE SPATIAL SIDE: contact blocked, and a place far from any neighbour.
branches.cn: 空间一面：联系被阻断，以及远离任何邻居的地方。

branches.en: THE STATISTICAL SIDE: one case standing outside any pattern.
branches.cn: 统计一面：一个案例处在任何模式之外。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL SIDE: a person with almost no human contact.
branches.cn: 社会一面：几乎没有人类接触的人。

branches.en: THE LABORATORY SIDE: a patient kept apart to stop spread, and a substance taken out of a mixture.
branches.cn: 实验室一面：为阻断传播而隔开的病人，以及从混合物中取出的物质。

branches.en: THE ENGINEERED SIDE: no conductive path, and a system that exchanges nothing with its surroundings.
branches.cn: 工程一面：没有导电路径，以及与外界不交换任何东西的系统。

intro.en: Isolated is a Latin participle built on insula 'island'; English adds the endings of state, agent and possibility.
intro.cn: isolated 是建立在 insula「岛」之上的拉丁分词；英语再加表示状态、施动与可能的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Insula 'island' gives insulatus 'made into an island'; Italian isolato and French isolé pass it to English as isolate and isolated.
latinIntro.cn: insula「岛」给出 insulatus「被造成岛的」；意大利语 isolato 与法语 isolé 把它传给英语，成为 isolate 与 isolated。

items.example: The noun is the picture behind every sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是每个义项背后的画面。

items.example: The participle is the direct source of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词是词族的直接来源。

items.example: The ending carries the participle into English.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把分词带入英语。

items.example: The verb names the act of cutting off.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词命名「切断联系」的动作。

items.example: The participle became the everyday adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词成了日常形容词。

items.example: The suffix gives isolation, the state of being apart.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀给出「隔离状态」。

items.example: The suffix gives isolator, the device.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀给出指装置的「隔离器」。

items.example: The suffix states that something can be separated out.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀说明某物可以被分离出来。

items.meaning: of an island; narrow in outlook
items.example: The same stem also gives a word for island narrowness.
items.exampleCN: 同一词干还给出表示「岛国狭隘」的词。

latinEntries.structure: insulatus, insulata, insulatum (participle used as adj.)

derivatives.zh: 由「使隔离」加动作名词后缀构成，义为「隔离状态」
由拉丁「岛」的形容词形式进入英语，义为「使隔离」
由「使隔离」加施动或器物后缀构成，义为「隔离器」
由「使隔离」加「可……的」后缀构成，义为「可隔离的」
由同一动词加更完整的「可……的」后缀构成，义为「可分离的」

definition_zh: 页边的；微小的；边缘化的；边际的；以微弱差距的；贫瘠边缘的；生态边缘的；次要的
definition_en: situated at or near an edge, or so small and slight that it barely matters
core_image: 书页正文之外那条窄窄的空白，写满了小字，正文反倒显得像主体
scene: 两种涂料刷在墙上，屋里的人来回看了半天，几乎分不出哪一种更浅。The difference between the two paints is marginal at best.
sceneCN: 这里指差别小到几乎可以忽略（第 2 个义项：数量上的差异极微小）；句意为这两种涂料的差别充其量也只是微乎其微。

derivatives.zh: 直接来自拉丁 margo「边缘」，是该形容词的词基，义为「页边；边缘；差额」
由该形容词加表示方式的副词后缀构成，义为「略微；以微弱差距」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词后缀构成，义为「边缘性；边缘地位」
由该形容词加表示「使……化」的动词后缀构成，义为「使边缘化」
由「使边缘化」的动词加表示动作结果的名词后缀构成，义为「边缘化」

senses.title: Written in the page margin
senses.definition: placed in the blank border of a page rather than in the main body of text
senses.definitionCN: 放在页面的空白边栏里，而不是正文之中
senses.example: A marginal note in pencil corrected the date.
senses.exampleCN: 一条铅笔写的页边注改正了日期。
senses.why: The Latin noun meant edge or border, and a page's border is its most literal margin.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词意为边缘或边界，书页的边栏就是最字面的「边缘」。

senses.title: So small it barely counts
senses.definition: very slight in amount or degree, close to the point of being unimportant
senses.definitionCN: 数量或程度上极小，接近无关紧要的地步
senses.example: The second product was only marginally cheaper.
senses.exampleCN: 第二件商品只是略微便宜一点。
senses.why: A difference at the edge of measurement sits just inside or outside the line, so it is barely worth counting.
senses.whyCN: 处于测量边缘的差异，正好贴着界线内外，因此几乎不值得计数。

senses.title: Pushed to the edge of society
senses.definition: having little power, representation or acceptance within a larger society
senses.definitionCN: 在更大的社会中缺少权力、代表性或接纳度
senses.example: The report focuses on marginal groups in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告关注城市里的边缘群体。
senses.why: People placed outside the main body of a society are located at its border, exactly where the word points.
senses.whyCN: 被置于社会主体之外的人，就处在它的边界上，正是这个词所指的位置。

senses.title: The next unit in economics
senses.titleCN: 经济学中再增加一单位
senses.definition: relating to the extra cost, benefit or utility of one additional unit
senses.definitionCN: 与再增加一个单位所带来的额外成本、收益或效用有关
senses.example: Marginal cost rises once the factory nears capacity.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂接近产能上限时，边际成本会上升。
senses.why: Economics looks at the change at the edge of existing output, and that edge is the margin.
senses.whyCN: 经济学看的是现有产出边缘处的变化，而那个边就是「边际」。

senses.title: Decided by a tiny gap
senses.definition: won or lost by a very small number of votes or points, so the result could easily change
senses.definitionCN: 以极少的票数或分数取胜或落败，结果很容易翻转
senses.example: The party holds a marginal seat by two hundred votes.
senses.exampleCN: 该党以两百票的优势握有一个边缘选区。
senses.why: A result sitting on the boundary between win and loss is marginal in the political sense.
senses.whyCN: 停在胜负边界上的结果，在政治意义上就是「边缘的」。

senses.title: Land at the limit of farming
senses.definition: land whose soil or position makes farming only barely profitable
senses.definitionCN: 土壤或位置使耕作只能勉强获利的土地
senses.example: Marginal land is often left to grazing.
senses.exampleCN: 边缘土地常被留作放牧。
senses.why: Such land lies at the edge of what can be cultivated, so it carries the edge word by position.
senses.whyCN: 这类土地处在可耕种的边缘，因此按位置得到「边缘」之名。

senses.title: A habitat at the edge of a range
senses.definition: a habitat where a species survives at the limit of its tolerated conditions
senses.definitionCN: 某物种在可忍受条件的极限处勉强存活的生境
senses.example: Marginal habitats hold fewer species but rare ones.
senses.exampleCN: 边缘生境物种较少，却常有珍稀种类。
senses.why: Ecology maps a range with a centre and a rim, and life at the rim lives on the margin.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把一个分布范围画成有中心有外围，住在外围的生命就处在边缘。

senses.title: Of secondary importance
senses.definition: playing a small or non-central part in a larger matter
senses.definitionCN: 在更大的事务中只起很小的、非核心的作用
senses.example: His role in the negotiation was marginal.
senses.exampleCN: 他在这场谈判中的作用很次要。
senses.why: Anything not in the main body of an affair is pushed to its edge, and the edge is where marginal things sit.
senses.whyCN: 不在事务主体之内的一切都被推到边上，而「边缘」正是这类事物所在之处。

intro.en: Marginal comes from Latin margo, marginis 'edge, border', through the adjective marginalis. English adopted it in the sixteenth century, and economics and politics later gave it precise uses. The Latin source is certain; the earlier origin of margo is reconstructed rather than attested.
intro.cn: marginal 来自拉丁 margo、marginis「边缘、边界」，经形容词 marginalis 进入英语，十六世纪被采用，后来经济学与政治学又赋予它精确用法。拉丁来源确定；margo 更早的来源属于重构，并未留下实证。

items.en: Margo meant edge, border or brink, and it named the rim of a page, a field or a sea.
items.cn: margo 意为边缘、边界或崖沿，可指书页、田地或海的边沿。

items.en: The pre-Latin source of margo is not settled, and proposals for its deeper root remain reconstructions rather than recorded forms.
items.cn: margo 在拉丁语之前的来源尚无定论，对其更深词根的种种设想仍属重构，而非有记录的形式。

items.en: Medieval Latin marginalis meant 'of the margin', first for writing placed at the edge of a page.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 marginalis 意为「页边的」，最初指写在页边上的文字。

items.en: English marginal began with page notes, then widened to anything at an edge or limit.
items.cn: 英语的这个词从页边注开始，随后扩展到任何处于边缘或极限的事物。

items.en: Nineteenth-century economics used marginal for the extra cost or benefit of one more unit, giving marginal cost and marginal utility.
items.cn: 十九世纪经济学用这个词指再加一单位的额外成本或收益，产生「边际成本」与「边际效用」。

items.en: A marginal seat is won by a small gap, and a marginal group sits outside the centre of a society.
items.cn: 边缘选区以极小差距决出；边缘群体处在社会中心之外。

note.en: The first group shares the edge stem; the second group holds words for smallness or secondary position, each with a different reason.
note.cn: 第一组共享「边缘」词干；第二组是表示微小或次要的词，各自的理由不同。

entries.definition: The blank edge of a page, or the amount by which one value exceeds another.
entries.definitionCN: 页面的空白边，或一个数值超出另一个的差额。

entries.definition: Slightly, or by a very small amount; it modifies comparisons.
entries.definitionCN: 略微，或以极小数量；修饰比较。

entries.definition: The condition of being at the edge of a group or system; a sociological noun.
entries.definitionCN: 处于群体或系统边缘的状况；是社会学的名词。

entries.definition: To push a person or group to the edge of influence; it names the act, not the state.
entries.definitionCN: 把人或群体推到影响力的边缘；命名动作，而非状态。

entries.definition: Small in degree; it measures amount only and says nothing about position at an edge.
entries.definitionCN: 程度上很小；只量数量，不涉及是否处于边缘。

entries.definition: Low in importance; it ranks things, while the target word places them at a border.
entries.definitionCN: 重要性低；对事物排序，而目标词把它们放到边界上。

entries.definition: On the outer edge of a system, often beside the main concern; close, but more spatial and less numerical.
entries.definitionCN: 处于系统的外缘，常在主关注点旁边；意思接近，但更偏空间而非数量。

entries.definition: So small that it can be disregarded; stronger than the target word, which still allows the difference to matter.
entries.definitionCN: 小到可以不理会；比目标词更强，因为目标词仍承认这点差别有意义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'edge': marginal things live at the edge of a page, a market or a society.
normal.cn: 词根意为「边缘」：边缘之物活在书页、市场或社会的边上。

normal.en: The family runs margin, marginally, marginality and marginalize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括页边、略微、边缘性、使边缘化。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark economics: marginal cost, marginal utility.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出经济学：边际成本、边际效用。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark politics and society: marginal seat, marginal group.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出政治与社会：边缘选区、边缘群体。

normal.en: Its neighbours differ: slight is only small, negligible is almost nothing.
normal.cn: 近邻有别：slight 只是小，negligible 几乎是零。

abstract.en: Picture a page whose margin is filled while the centre stays blank.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸边栏写满，正文却空着。

abstract.en: Picture a runner finishing one stride behind the winner.
abstract.cn: 想象一个跑者比冠军差一步冲线。

abstract.en: Picture a town so close to the border that the sign is on its main street.
abstract.cn: 想象一座小镇贴着边界，界牌就立在主街上。

examples.en: The effect on test scores was marginal.
examples.cn: 对考试成绩的影响微乎其微。

examples.en: Marginal notes in the old book show how it was read.
examples.cn: 这本旧书上的页边注显示了它曾被怎样阅读。

examples.en: The policy did little for marginal communities.
examples.cn: 这项政策对边缘群体帮助甚微。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马挤脑」——马挤在栅栏最边上，只占一线之地，就是边缘的

root: 拉丁 margo、marginis「边缘、边界」→ 中世纪拉丁 marginalis「页边的」→ 英语 marginal；margo 更早的来源属重构，尚未确证。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all place something at an edge: the rim of a page, the limit of significance, the border of society, the next unit of output, the line between win and loss, land or habitat at a limit, and a secondary role.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把某物放在边缘上：书页的边、意义的临界、社会的边界、产出的下一单位、胜负的分界、处于极限的土地或生境，以及次要的角色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow strip at the border, where a thing sits just inside the line.
core.cn: 核心意象：边界上一条窄带，事物正贴着界线内侧。

branches.en: THE PAGE SENSE: writing placed in the blank border.
branches.cn: 书页义：写在空白边栏里的文字。

branches.en: THE NUMERICAL EDGE: a difference barely worth counting, and a result decided by a tiny gap.
branches.cn: 数量边缘：几乎不值得计数的差别，以及以极小差距决出的结果。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL EDGE: people outside the centre of a society.
branches.cn: 社会边缘：处在社会中心之外的人。

branches.en: THE ECONOMIC EDGE: the extra cost or benefit of one more unit.
branches.cn: 经济边缘：再加一单位的额外成本或收益。

branches.en: THE LIMITS OF USE: land barely worth farming, habitat barely survivable, and a role barely central.
branches.cn: 使用极限：勉强可耕的地、勉强能活的生境，以及勉强算核心的角色。

intro.en: Marginal is built on Latin margo 'edge' with the adjective ending -al; English adds endings for manner, state and the act of pushing to the edge.
intro.cn: marginal 建立在拉丁 margo「边缘」与形容词词尾 -al 之上；英语再加表示方式、状态与「推至边缘」动作的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Margo, marginis 'edge' gives the stem margin-, and Medieval Latin marginalis gives the adjective; English margin also comes from the same noun.
latinIntro.cn: margo、marginis「边缘」给出词干 margin-，中世纪拉丁 marginalis 给出形容词；英语的 margin 也出自同一名词。

items.example: The noun is the origin of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整个词族的来源。

items.example: The stem appears in margin and marginal.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干出现在 margin 与 marginal 中。

items.example: The ending makes an adjective of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词变成形容词。

items.example: It first described writing in a page margin.
items.exampleCN: 它最初描述写在页边的文字。

items.example: English widened it to economics and society.
items.exampleCN: 英语把它扩展到经济学与社会。

items.example: The noun kept both the page and the arithmetic senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词同时保留书页与算术两义。

items.example: The suffix makes the comparison adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成比较副词。

items.example: The suffix names the condition of being at the edge.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名「处于边缘」的状况。

items.example: The suffix names the act of pushing to the edge.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名「推到边缘」的动作。

items.example: The suffix names the process as a whole.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名整个过程。

derivatives.zh: 直接来自拉丁 margo，义为「页边；差额」
由该形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「略微」
由该形容词加性质名词后缀构成，义为「边缘性」
由该形容词加「使……化」的动词后缀构成，义为「使边缘化」
由「使边缘化」加动作名词后缀构成，义为「边缘化」

definition_zh: 巨大的；沉重的；大量的；严重的；体格魁梧的；块状的（岩体）；大面积的（病变）；厚重的（建筑）
definition_en: very large in size, weight or amount, often so large that it is striking or hard to deal with
core_image: 港口边立着一整块从山体切下的石料，旁边的卡车小得像个玩具
scene: 港口入口立着一整块从山体切下的石料，旁边的卡车小得像个玩具。A massive block of granite now stands at the harbour entrance.
sceneCN: 这里指体积巨大、分量惊人（第 1 个义项：形体或体量极大）；句意为一块巨大的花岗岩石料如今立在港口入口处。

derivatives.zh: 直接来自拉丁 massa「团块」，是该形容词的词基，义为「团块；大量；群众的」
由该形容词加表示方式的副词后缀构成，义为「巨大地；极其」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词后缀构成，义为「巨大；沉重感」
由「团块」加表示动作或集合的名词后缀构成，义为「体量组合」，是建筑用语
由同一词根经法语进入英语，义为「山块；地块」，指连成整体的一组山体

senses.title: Very large in size
senses.definition: occupying far more space than ordinary objects of its kind, so that it dominates a view
senses.definitionCN: 占据的空间远大于同类常见物体，因而在视野中占主导
senses.example: A massive crane lifted the bridge section into place.
senses.exampleCN: 一台巨大的起重机把桥段吊装到位。
senses.why: The Latin noun meant a lump or a mass, so the adjective first describes sheer bulk.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词意为「团块、一堆」，因此这个形容词首先描述的是纯粹的体量。

senses.title: Heavy and solid
senses.definition: thick and weighty, made of material that feels hard to move
senses.definitionCN: 厚而重，由让人感到难以搬动的材料做成
senses.example: The altar is a massive slab of stone.
senses.exampleCN: 祭坛是一整块沉重的石板。
senses.why: A mass has weight as well as size, so the adjective carries both impressions at once.
senses.whyCN: 团块既有体积也有重量，因此这个形容词同时带着两种感受。

senses.title: Huge in amount
senses.definition: present in a very large quantity, said of data, sums, effort or numbers of people
senses.definitionCN: 以极大的数量存在，用于数据、金额、努力或人数
senses.example: The archive holds a massive amount of correspondence.
senses.exampleCN: 这间档案馆藏有大量往来信件。
senses.why: Amounts can pile up like material, and a heap that keeps growing becomes a mass.
senses.whyCN: 数量可以像材料一样堆积，越堆越高的那一堆就成了「团块」。

senses.title: Extremely serious in effect
senses.definition: very great in severity, so that recovery or repair is difficult
senses.definitionCN: 严重程度极大，以至于恢复或修复都很困难
senses.example: The earthquake caused massive damage to the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 地震给老城造成了严重破坏。
senses.why: Damage has size too, and damage of enormous size is expressed with the word for bulk.
senses.whyCN: 破坏也有「大小」，巨大规模的破坏就用表示体量的词来表达。

senses.title: Broad and heavy in build
senses.definition: having a large, solid body, said of a person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 身体大而结实，用于人或动物
senses.example: A massive guard stood at the gate all night.
senses.exampleCN: 一名魁梧的守卫整夜站在门口。
senses.why: A body can have the same solid bulk as a stone block, and English applies the word to people.
senses.whyCN: 身体可以有和石块一样厚实的体量，英语便把这个词用在人身上。

senses.title: Formed as one unbroken rock body
senses.definition: in geology, said of rock that has no visible bedding or layering, appearing as one solid mass
senses.definitionCN: 地质学中用于看不出层理、呈一整块的岩石
senses.example: The cliff is cut into massive granite with no clear layers.
senses.exampleCN: 这面崖壁由无明显层理的整块花岗岩构成。
senses.why: Geology uses the word for rock that behaves as a single lump rather than as stacked sheets.
senses.whyCN: 地质学用这个词指表现得像一整块、而不是叠层薄片的岩石。

senses.title: Very extensive in medicine
senses.definition: said of a bleed, clot or infarct that covers a large part of an organ
senses.definitionCN: 用于覆盖器官很大一部分的出血、血栓或梗死
senses.example: He survived a massive heart attack last winter.
senses.exampleCN: 去年冬天他挺过了一次大面积心肌梗死。
senses.why: Clinical language measures lesions by extent, and an extent near the whole organ is massive.
senses.whyCN: 临床按范围量度病灶，范围接近整个器官的就称为「大面积」。

senses.title: Thick and plain in construction
senses.definition: built with heavy walls and simple, undecorated forms, often of stone
senses.definitionCN: 以厚重墙体与简洁无装饰的形式建造，常用石材
senses.example: The cathedral's massive walls were built to last centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这座主教座堂的厚重墙体是为挺过数百年而建的。
senses.why: Architecture judges weight and simplicity together, and a building that shows its mass is called massive.
senses.whyCN: 建筑把重量与简洁一起评价，一座显露自身质量的建筑就被称为「厚重」。

intro.en: Massive comes from Latin massa 'lump, mass', itself from Greek maza 'barley cake', through French massif. English adopted it in the sixteenth century, and geology, medicine and architecture later gave it precise uses.
intro.cn: massive 来自拉丁 massa「团块、一堆」，后者源于希腊 maza「大麦饼」，经法语 massif 进入英语，十六世纪被采用；地质、医学与建筑后来赋予它精确用法。

items.en: Maza named a kneaded barley cake, a single shapeless lump of dough, and the image of one solid mass began there.
items.cn: maza 指揉成的大麦饼，是一团没有形状的面团，「一整块实体」的画面由此开始。

items.en: Massa meant a lump, a mass or a body of material, and it also gave English mass.
items.cn: massa 意为团块、一堆或一团材料，也给出英语的 mass。

items.en: French massif described something solid and bulky, and English took the adjective in that form.
items.cn: 法语 massif 形容坚实而笨重的东西，英语照这个形式引入形容词。

items.en: English massive first described heavy objects and bodies, then extended to amounts and effects.
items.cn: 英语的这个词先形容沉重的物体与身体，后扩展到数量与后果。

items.en: Geology uses massive for rock without bedding, and architecture for walls that display their weight.
items.cn: 地质学用这个词指无层理的岩石，建筑用指显露自身重量的墙。

items.en: Clinical writing measures an infarct or bleed by how much of an organ it covers, and a very large one is massive.
items.cn: 临床文字按覆盖器官的多少来量度梗死或出血，覆盖很大的就称为大面积。

note.en: The first group shares the lump stem; the second group holds size words that differ in scale, shape or tone.
note.cn: 第一组共享「团块」词干；第二组是表示大小的词，在规模、形状或语气上各有不同。

entries.definition: A quantity of matter, or a large number of people; the noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 一定量的物质，或一大群人；是形容词背后的名词。

entries.definition: To an enormous degree; it often modifies verbs such as increase or build.
entries.definitionCN: 达到巨大程度；常修饰「增加」「建造」一类动词。

entries.definition: The quality of being huge and heavy; a state noun used in description.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大而沉重的性质；是用于描写的状态名词。

entries.definition: The arrangement of volumes in a building; an architectural term from the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑中各体量的组合；同一词干来的建筑术语。

entries.definition: Very big; the general word, without the suggestion of solid weight.
entries.definitionCN: 非常大；通用词，不带「坚实沉重」的暗示。

entries.definition: Extremely large; it stresses scale beyond expectation rather than mass.
entries.definitionCN: 极大；强调超出预期的规模，而非质量。

entries.definition: Large and awkward to move because of shape; it adds inconvenience to size.
entries.definitionCN: 因形状而大得难以搬动；在「大」之外多了不便。

entries.definition: Astonishingly large, as a giant statue; it carries awe rather than weight.
entries.definitionCN: 大到惊人，如巨型雕像；带惊叹意味，而非重量感。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means a lump: massive things come as one solid block.
normal.cn: 词根意为「团块」：巨大的东西是一整块实心的。

normal.en: The family runs mass, massively, massiveness and massing.
normal.cn: 同族词包括团块、巨大地、巨大、体量组合。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark quantity and severity: massive amount, massive damage.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出数量与严重程度：大量、严重破坏。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark science: massive rock, massive heart attack.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出科学用法：块状岩体、大面积心肌梗死。

normal.en: Its neighbours differ: huge is general, bulky adds awkwardness, colossal adds awe.
normal.cn: 近邻有别：huge 是通用词，bulky 多了笨重，colossal 多了惊叹。

abstract.en: Picture a single stone so large that a road bends around it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块大到公路要绕着走的石头。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd so thick that no one can cross it.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人多到没人能穿过去。

abstract.en: Picture a door whose frame alone weighs more than a car.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，光是门框就比一辆车重。

examples.en: The company made a massive investment in new machinery.
examples.cn: 这家公司在新机器上投入了巨额资金。

examples.en: A massive storm shut down every ferry in the region.
examples.cn: 一场猛烈的风暴让该地区所有渡轮停运。

examples.en: The cathedral's massive walls have stood for six hundred years.
examples.cn: 这座主教座堂厚重的墙已经立了六百年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马四伏」——四匹马伏在一起才拉得动，形容巨大沉重

root: 希腊 maza「大麦饼、一团面团」→ 拉丁 massa「团块」→ 法语 massif → 英语 massive；同族 mass、massif、massing。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe one solid bulk: an object in space, weight in the hand, a growing quantity, the scale of damage, a body, a rock body, a lesion, or a wall.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述同一团实在的体量：空间里的物体、手里的重量、不断增大的数量、破坏的规模、身体、岩体、病灶，或一堵墙。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one shapeless lump so big that it dominates whatever stands beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一大团没有形状的实体，大到让它旁边的一切都显得渺小。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL BASE: a large object and its solid weight.
branches.cn: 物理基础：庞大的物体与其坚实的重量。

branches.en: THE QUANTITATIVE FORM: a heap of data, money or people.
branches.cn: 数量形态：一堆数据、金钱或人。

branches.en: THE SEVERITY FORM: damage on a scale that is hard to repair.
branches.cn: 严重形态：难以修复的大规模破坏。

branches.en: THE HUMAN FORM: a broad, heavy body.
branches.cn: 人的形态：宽厚沉重的身体。

branches.en: THE TECHNICAL FORMS: rock without bedding, a lesion covering much of an organ, and walls that show their weight.
branches.cn: 技术形态：无层理的岩体、覆盖器官大部的病灶，以及显露重量的墙。

intro.en: Massive rests on Latin massa 'lump' and the adjective ending -ive; English adds endings for manner, state and architectural arrangement.
intro.cn: massive 建立在拉丁 massa「团块」与形容词词尾 -ive 之上；英语再加表示方式、状态与建筑组合的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin massa 'lump' gives English mass directly; Medieval Latin massivus and French massif give the adjective massive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 massa「团块」直接给出英语 mass；中世纪拉丁 massivus 与法语 massif 给出形容词 massive。

items.example: The noun is the origin of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是词族的来源。

items.meaning: a body of matter; a great number
items.example: The noun kept both the physical and social senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词同时保留物理与社会两义。

items.example: The ending makes a describing word of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词变成描述词。

items.example: The medieval form passed through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个中世纪形式经法语传下。

items.example: English extended it to amounts and severity.
items.exampleCN: 英语把它扩展到数量与严重程度。

items.example: The suffix gives the degree adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀给出程度副词。

items.example: The suffix names the quality of bulk.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名「体量巨大」的性质。

items.example: The noun names a geological mass of rock.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名地质上的岩块。

items.example: The ending builds the architectural term massing.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀造出建筑术语「体量组合」。

items.example: The adverb modifies verbs of growth and spending.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词修饰「增长」「开支」类动词。

derivatives.zh: 直接来自拉丁 massa，义为「团块；大量」
由该形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「巨大地」
由该形容词加性质名词后缀构成，义为「巨大」
由词根加动作名词后缀构成，义为「体量组合」
由同一词根经法语进入英语，义为「山块」
